title: The .NET 8-to-10 pair is carved out of the DW-078 sweep into its own row DW-080; DW-066's minimal-base move rides with the aspnet FROM-line change as ONE base-image decision, and DW-066 is Activated because its trigger has demonstrably fired
decision:
d1 - #128 (dotnet/sdk 8.0 to 10.0) AND #134 (dotnet/aspnet 8.0 to 10.0) ARE CARVED OUT OF THE SWEEP. DW-078's sweep covers the remaining TEN pull requests. The pair moves to DW-080 as its own work with its own activation trigger. REASON THIS WAS RE-ASKED AT ALL: DEC-072 d1's 'sweep everything, majors included' was answered over a description of the queue that did not contain these two rows, because the command behind that description was capped at --limit 10 and they sat past position ten (PE-599). The solution targets net8.0, so this is a RUNTIME MIGRATION touching target frameworks, analyzers, EF Core and the container base at once - not a dependency bump - and folding it into a hygiene sweep would put a migration underneath every other failure in the batch. That is the same attribution argument DEC-073 used to put the sweep before SL-033, applied one level down. THE OPERATOR'S EARLIER 'EVERYTHING' IS NOT BEING REINTERPRETED BY THE AGENT: it was re-put to them with the corrected facts and they carved the pair out.

d2 - DW-066 IS ACTIVATED, AND THE MINIMAL-BASE MOVE RIDES WITH THE aspnet FROM-LINE CHANGE AS ONE BASE-IMAGE DECISION. Whenever those lines are touched, api and worker move to alpine or distroless in the SAME change rather than merging a Debian-to-Debian bump and reopening the file later. DW-066's own trigger names this as the moment: 'whenever a base-image bump is being made anyway (Dependabot docker updates touch these lines)'. #134 edits deploy/Dockerfile.backend lines 31 and 51, and #128 edits line 16 - verified by gh pr view --json files, not inferred. THE TRIGGER HAD FIRED AND THE AGENT HAD SAID IT HAD NOT, earlier in the same session, reasoning from the truncated listing that the open docker rows touched only node, nginx and mssql. CONSEQUENCE: DW-080 carries both the runtime migration and the minimal-base move, and NFR-054's minimal-base clause becomes evidenceable for the first time - it cannot record Met while api and worker sit on a Debian base, and DW-066 is the only route to an acceptance criterion for that clause. THE RISK IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOT THE EDIT: alpine is musl rather than glibc, this application talks to SQL Server through native interop and does culture-aware work in Arabic and English, and globalization plus native loading is exactly where musl breaks. It must go through the full e2e leg with Arabic FREETEXT verified end to end; a green unit suite proves nothing, because the failure mode compiles and unit-tests perfectly.
rationale:
d1: a framework major and a base-image major landing inside a queue-clearing batch is the attribution problem twice over. Carving the pair out costs a second batch and buys a clean answer to 'what broke'. It also means the ten-PR sweep stays what DEC-073 scheduled - a short, mechanical batch that unblocks SL-033 - rather than becoming a migration that delays the slice indefinitely.

d2: the row itself argued this before anyone asked. Its trigger was written to catch precisely the moment when the expensive part of the change - opening the Dockerfile, re-running the full e2e leg, re-verifying Arabic FREETEXT - is already being paid for by something else. Merging #134 alone would spend that cost on a Debian-to-Debian move and leave the minimal-base clause exactly where it was, with the next opportunity unknown. Doing both at once is the cheaper total even though it is the larger single change, and NFR-054's clause was KEPT rather than relaxed precisely so that it would eventually be satisfied rather than argued away.

title: DW-082 is closed by writing the missing handler tests before #307 merges; ALL FOUR activated streams are in scope; the leaked vite processes are killed and the gap that let them leak is filed; three of this session's findings become lesson rows
decision:
d1 - DW-082 IS CLOSED BY WRITING THE MISSING TESTS, NOT BY MOVING THE THRESHOLD OR REFUSING THE UPGRADE. The experiment settled that coverage-v8 v4 is the honest counter: on ErrorBoundary.tsx, both providers record the SAME uncalled inline onClick on line 30, and they differ only in where they count it - v3 has no zero-hit statements so the line is credited, v4 records statement 3 at zero hits and that propagates into the line metric. Since ADR-0016's gate is lines only, v3 renders every untested inline handler invisible to it. The twenty files were never properly covered. So the route is: identify each affected file's uncovered lines the same way the experiment did, write tests that actually invoke those handlers, and merge #307 once the gate passes honestly. THIS IS THE ONLY ROUTE THAT ENDS WITH BOTH A CURRENT vitest AND A TRUE 95%. #307, #261 and #137 stay open until it does; #307 supersedes the other two in content and closing it would lose the paired bump.

d2 - ALL FOUR ACTIVATED STREAMS ARE IN SCOPE. The operator's answer to 'what runs next' was ALL: the DW-082 handler tests, SL-033 beginning at WBS-24.1, DW-080 (the .NET 8-to-10 migration carrying DW-066's alpine move), and DW-079 (the NFR-018 ASVS evidence pack). NOTHING IS DESELECTED. ⚠ THE ORDER IS NOT SETTLED BY THAT ANSWER and the sequence below is the AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, recorded as such so a later session does not read it as the operator's instruction, and freely reorderable by them: (1) the DW-082 handler tests, because SL-033 will add new components with new inline handlers and doing this first means WBS-24.1's own code lands under a gate that can see them; (2) SL-033 from WBS-24.1 in DEC-071 d1's order; (3) DW-080 ALONE with nothing else in flight, which its own row requires - it is a migration with a musl-and-globalization failure mode a unit suite cannot see; (4) DW-079, document-only and slottable anywhere.

d3 - THE SIX LEAKED vite PROCESSES ARE KILLED AND THE GAP THAT LET THEM LEAK IS FILED. Six vite dev servers plus their six npx parents, all rooted in src/Acmp.Web/node_modules on ports 5199, 5201, 5233, 5241, 4173 and 8124, the oldest thirteen days old, were holding rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node open - which is why npm ci failed on the host with EPERM and EBUSY and why an earlier npm ci gutted node_modules midway. They were re-enumerated immediately before killing rather than taken from a stale list, and nothing outside that set was touched; 65 unrelated node processes were left running. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, and it is why a row follows rather than just a kill: trap 28 covers leftover visual-verify FILES - a vr-*.tsx in src/ that would ship - and nothing covered leaked PROCESSES, which is exactly why these survived thirteen days across multiple sessions while a file-level guard ran clean.

d4 - THREE OF THIS SESSION'S FINDINGS BECOME LESSON ROWS, born Proposed. The operator selected: the instrument-changed finding, the shared-mechanism refinement of LL-009, and the base-image-versus-package-repo coupling. They are written Proposed rather than Approved because approved lessons are IMMUTABLE in this store and the operator has chosen the findings but not yet read the final wording; confirming the text is a separate, deliberate act. The fourth candidate - that a discovery guard converts a broken instrument's silent false-pass into a loud false-fail - was NOT selected and is not filed; it restates trap 31 with new evidence rather than adding a rule.
rationale:
d1: the experiment inverted the row's own framing, which is why it was worth running. The twenty red files looked like a regression caused by a tool change; they are a pre-existing gap the old tool concealed. Lowering the threshold was already forbidden and is now more so - the number would be hiding real untested code rather than an artefact. Refusing the upgrade on the grounds that v4 miscounts is no longer supportable.

d2: recording 'all' as scope while marking the order as the agent's keeps two things separate that are easy to conflate - what the operator decided, and what the agent inferred about how to do it. DEC-071 d3 set the precedent that an operator's container choice is recorded as theirs and the agent's disagreement recorded as the agent's; this is the same discipline applied to sequencing rather than to slicing.

d3: the kill is trivially reversible and the row is the durable half. A cleanup that is not part of the loop that creates the mess will not happen; that is the same reasoning that put the base-image coupling note into the Dockerfile rather than only into a register row.

d4: immutability is the whole reason for Proposed. LL-011's own history shows what a lesson costs when its wording has to be superseded rather than edited, and the operator selecting a finding is not the same as approving a sentence.
source_span: Operator interview 2026-08-23 (third round), run at the operator's request after DW-078 closed and the DW-082 experiment returned its verdict. Each question carried the cited records' own text inline per LL-011.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-25: ALL FIVE PENDING LESSONS APPROVED AND PINNED; #137 CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED; THE AGENT'S STREAM ORDER ACCEPTED; ASM-011 CARRIED DELIBERATELY
decision:
d1 - ALL FIVE LESSONS ARE APPROVED AND PINNED: LL-017, LL-018, LL-019, LL-020, LL-021. Pinned means each is rendered into the tool-owned note the agent loads at startup; approved means each is now IMMUTABLE - the store refuses an edit, so a change requires a superseding row.

d2 - PR #137 (@vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.6 to 4.1.10) IS CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED. Its content landed at a higher version (4.1.11) via #307, so closing it finishes DEC-072 d1's sweep rather than opening a new question. The agent had deliberately left it alone as an outward action nobody had asked for; the operator directed the close.

d3 - THE REMAINING STREAM ORDER IS ACCEPTED AS THE AGENT RECOMMENDED IT: SL-033 from WBS-24.1, then DW-080 alone with nothing else in flight, then DW-079. This is acceptance of a recommendation, not an independent instruction - DEC-075 d2's point stands that all four streams were in scope and the ORDER was the agent's to propose and the operator's to accept.

d4 - ASM-011 IS CARRIED DELIBERATELY AND ITS ADVISORY STAYS RED. The urgency SLA thresholds were never validated with the committee and the validation date has passed. The operator declined to re-date it, to escalate it to a risk, and to mark it validated. The red is the control working: a decayed assumption is supposed to look decayed, and clearing the date to restore the amber would re-blind the control that was deliberately fixed on 2026-08-20.
rationale:
CONTEXT. Five lessons stood Proposed with lessons-confirmed failing on purpose. Nothing else awaited the operator - no Proposed decisions, ADRs, scope changes or open questions. LL-017/018/019 came from DEC-075 d4, where the operator had selected the FINDINGS and explicitly had NOT read the sentences they were written up in; LL-020 and LL-021 were recorded by the agent on 2026-08-25 against its own mistakes, which is why their framing was flagged to the operator as the most likely to be self-serving.

FORM. The slate was put as a generated docket carrying the full canonical text of every field of every row - statement, context, recommendation, rationale and both impact clauses - printed from data/lessons.jsonl, HTML-escaped, with an independent verifier confirming all 30 blocks appeared byte-identical in the output. That form is LL-011's requirement, and the generator is committed as scripts/gen-lesson-docket.mjs so the next lessons interview is compliant by default rather than by remembering.

WHY EACH WAY. On d1 the operator approved every sentence AS WRITTEN rather than refining any - the outcome the full-text form exists to make possible, the previous interview having been refused precisely because ids alone gave the reader nothing to adjudicate. On d2 the sweep authority already existed and a superseded-but-open PR is ambient state a later session would have spent time re-deriving. On d3 the sequencing reasons held: doing DW-082 first meant SL-033's new components land under a gate that can SEE their inline handlers, and DW-080 needs the isolation its own row demands. On d4 the operator has now declined three times to relax or clear a decayed control, consistent with DEC-066 and SC-024 - the register states the target, not the status quo.

⚠ THE APPROVAL PATH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS A REAL CONTROL. The store refuses an approving upsert whose content differs by even one character from the stored row - 'approval/promotion is not an edit - content drifted on [...]; send the stored content byte-identical, or supersede first' - and it separately refuses one without confirmed_by, because attribution lands WITH approval and can never be added later. Between them these make LL-001's dangerous middle safe here: re-typing a long field in order to preserve it fails LOUDLY instead of silently enshrining a corrupted immutable lesson.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-25 (SECOND ROUND): DEF-108 CARRIED OPEN AT HIGH SEVERITY WITH READINESS FALSE; `scripts/**` CARVED OUT OF THE DIRECT-TO-MAIN RULE *AND* A POST-PUSH CI CHECK MANDATED; EVERY RED FROM THE FTS TEST IS REAL; A CONTAINER-STARTUP TIMEOUT GOES IN FIRST, BEFORE WBS-24.1
decision:
d1 - DEF-108 IS CARRIED **OPEN AT HIGH SEVERITY**, with a recurrence trigger, and `readiness_check` therefore returns **ready:FALSE** until it is chased. **THIS OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to convert it to a deferred-work row so readiness could return TRUE. The operator chose the strictest available option and the blocking consequence is accepted deliberately, not overlooked: nothing may be declared done at package scope while it stands.

d2 - THE BRANCHING RULE IS AMENDED IN **BOTH** DIRECTIONS, which was also stricter than either single option offered. (a) STRUCTURAL: anything touching `scripts/**` goes branch -> PR -> green CI -> squash-merge, like any other code. It is no longer covered by the direct-to-main allowance. (b) DISCIPLINARY: after **ANY** direct push to `main`, CI is polled to completion - `status` until `completed`, then `conclusion` - regardless of what the commit touched. ⚠ Adding `scripts/**` to the workflows' path-ignore was explicitly REJECTED and must not be proposed again: several `scripts/*.mjs` ARE the CI gates (check-coverage, check-i18n, check-vulns, check-hardcoded-strings), so ignoring that path would mean a change to a gate never runs the gate.

d3 - A RED FROM `SearchProvidersFtsTests` IS TREATED AS **REAL**: stop and investigate. Re-running to see whether it passes is NOT the response. **ALSO STRICTER THAN THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to re-run once and log the occurrence. The reasoning the operator's choice rests on is in the register already: that test is the ONLY place any FREETEXT branch executes against real SQL Server, so it is the single test whose silent loss would be least visible and most expensive.

d4 - A CONTAINER-STARTUP TIMEOUT IS ADDED INSIDE THE TEST so a hung container fails fast with a legible message instead of burning the backend job's 25-minute ceiling and reporting 'cancelled' - a verdict that is neither pass nor fail and reads like a fluke.

d5 - THAT WORK RUNS **FIRST, BEFORE `WBS-24.1`**, amending DEC-076 d3's order. `SL-033` would otherwise run CI repeatedly against an unfixed intermittent while d3 requires stopping on every red from it, so the slice would be interrupted by exactly the ambiguous signal d4 exists to remove. The revised order is: container-startup timeout -> `SL-033` from `WBS-24.1` -> `DW-080` alone -> `DW-079`.
rationale:
EVIDENCE THE INTERVIEW RESTED ON, gathered before the questions were asked (LL-008: sweep BEFORE the interview, not after). Four data points on backend code that did not change between them: 8432a1d SUCCESS in 9 minutes; 6bdaac4 FAILURE with the SQL Server container dying at startup ('Failed to load LSA: 0xc0070102', 'fatal error 0xC0000001') while Domain 269, Architecture 54, Application 1167 and Api 368 all passed; 6acbb89 CANCELLED after the backend job hit its own timeout-minutes: 25; and a plain re-run of that identical tree SUCCESS on all four jobs. A keyword sweep across defects, deferred-work, decisions, ADRs, open questions, risks, requirements and assumptions found NOTHING covering intermittent Testcontainers SQL Server startup - this is new ground, not a known issue.

WHY THE OVERRIDES ARE RECORDED AS OVERRIDES. DEC-071 d3 set the precedent that what the operator DECIDED is kept separate from what the agent INFERRED, and that reasoning-against is preserved rather than quietly harmonised. The agent argued that two reds sandwiched between greens on unchanged code points at the runner's ability to start SQLPAL rather than at this repository, and that a DW- row would keep the observation visible without holding readiness false. The operator's position is the one the register already endorses in three other places: the register states the TARGET, not the status quo, and this project has now declined four separate times to relax or clear a control that had gone red.

WHAT PROMPTED d2, and it is the agent's own failure. The DEC-076 commit was pushed, `git status` was run, the package was closed and the state was reported to the operator as clean WITHOUT `gh run list` ever being run - and that commit had turned `main` red. The exemption being relied on did not cover the commit being made: the direct-to-main allowance exists because both workflows path-ignore `tamheed-package/**` and `.claude/**`, but `scripts/*.py` and `scripts/*.mjs` are not ignored, and the agent had been deliberately committing such instruments all session. A 'docs-only' commit carrying an instrument runs the full pipeline. The operator closed the gap structurally AND behaviourally rather than choosing between the two.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-26 (AFTER `DW-084`): `LL-022` APPROVED AND PINNED; `DW-085` ACTIVATED AND INSERTED BEFORE `WBS-24.1`; `WBS-24.1` STARTS IN THE SAME SESSION. TWO OF THE THREE OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION.
decision:
d1 - `LL-022` IS APPROVED AND PINNED, every sentence as written, none refined. The agent deliberately offered NO recommendation on this one, on the ground that it is the agent's own sentence and `DEC-075` d4 established that selecting a finding is not approving the wording it was written up in. The operator read the full canonical text on the docket and took it as written. `lessons-confirmed` returns to pass.

d2 - `DW-085` IS ACTIVATED AND RUNS BEFORE `WBS-24.1`. **THIS OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to CARRY it Open on the ground that its trigger has not fired - nothing has ever been observed hanging in the FTS image build, and all four `DEF-108` data points name container startup rather than the build. The operator took the option the agent argued against, as they have now done three times in three interviews.

d3 - `WBS-24.1` STARTS IN THIS SAME SESSION, after `DW-085`. **ALSO AN OVERRIDE**: the agent recommended handing off to a fresh session with `prompts/slice-kickoff.md`, on the ground that an eight-item slice deserves a full context window and this one was long and expensive. The operator chose to continue.

THE REVISED ORDER IS THEREFORE: `DW-085` -> `SL-033` from `WBS-24.1` -> `DW-080` alone -> `DW-079`. This AMENDS `DEC-077` d5, exactly as d5 itself amended `DEC-076` d3, and `SC-034` carries the row delta.

⚠ WHAT d2 DOES NOT CHANGE, recorded so the next session does not read the activation as wider than it is: `DW-085` still cannot be proven the way `DW-084` was. Its own row says forcing an image-build hang would need a deliberately-hanging Dockerfile committed to the repository. The evidence for it will therefore be weaker than `DW-084`'s, and the row must say so rather than borrow `DW-084`'s standard of proof.
rationale:
EVIDENCE THE INTERVIEW RESTED ON, gathered BEFORE the questions were asked (`LL-008`: sweep before the interview, not after). A keyword sweep across acceptance criteria, decisions, defects, deferred work, document sections, lessons, requirements, risks and scope changes - on image build, CreateAsync, Dockerfile.sqlserver, docker build, cold build, image cache, 3.62, timeout-minutes, 25-minute and startup timeout - found NOTHING already covering an image-BUILD hang. The hits were all adjacent rather than overlapping: `AC-086` is ECR publication by OIDC, `DW-059` is the `NFR-054` image-size measurement that is the SOURCE of the 3.62 GB figure, and the `SEC-` hits are narrative sections mentioning the words in unrelated contexts. `DW-085` is new ground.

THE FORM OF THE SLATE, because it is what made the interview possible. Every record the operator read to decide carried its own full canonical text, printed from the JSONL by a generator and verified byte-identical before publishing - fifteen fields across `LL-022`, `DW-085`, `DW-084` and `DEC-077`. That discharges `LL-011` mechanically rather than by remembering it. The verifier was itself calibrated with two injected faults - one changed character, one emptied field - and detected both, so the clean pass is a result rather than a silence (`LL-013`).

WHY THE OVERRIDES ARE RECORDED AS OVERRIDES. `DEC-071` d3 set the precedent that what the operator DECIDED stays separate from what the agent INFERRED, and that reasoning-against is preserved rather than quietly harmonised into agreement. The agent's case for carrying `DW-085` was that an unfired trigger is the honest state and that spending a CI cycle on a hazard nobody has observed inverts the register's own discipline. The operator's position has a counter the agent itself put on the docket: the helper pattern exists right now and the context is warm, so doing it later costs re-entry - and this project has twice before judged that a warm context is worth more than a strict reading of a trigger.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT RAISED, stated so the silence is not read as an oversight. `DEF-108` was settled the previous day, the operator took the strictest available option, and nothing new has occurred - no new occurrence, and `DW-084` explicitly does not close it, so re-asking would have been offering a narrowing already declined. `ASM-011` stays red on purpose; it has a real outstanding action behind it - the urgency SLA thresholds need validating with the committee - but its text was not on the docket, and asking the operator to decide a record they had not been shown is the exact failure `LL-011` exists to prevent.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-26 (SECOND ROUND, AFTER `WBS-24.1`): `LL-023` APPROVED AND PINNED; `DEF-110` CARRIED - RECORD IT, CHANGE NOTHING; `WBS-24.1` ADJUDICATED PER-ITEM TO `Implemented`; `WBS-24.2` STARTS IN THE SAME SESSION.
decision:
d1 - `LL-023` IS APPROVED AND PINNED, every sentence as written. The agent again offered NO recommendation on its own lesson and said plainly that its enthusiasm for a lesson about its own failure mode should be discounted. `lessons-confirmed` returns to pass, and `handoff_emit` ran in the SAME batch with the rebuilt note READ BACK to confirm `LL-023` reached it as pinned - `DEF-107` discharged by observation rather than by assuming the emit worked.

d2 - `DEF-110` IS CARRIED OPEN: **record it, change nothing.** This is the disposition the operator chose for `DEF-102`, applied to what is structurally the same thing - a register row asserting a capability the code does not have. The row stays `Open`/medium in the `defects-minor` advisory so it is visible rather than silent. The agent recommended this and the operator agreed; the counter-argument was put on the docket rather than withheld, namely that `ASM-011`'s own `risk_if_wrong` says the thresholds *"must be redesigned before PH-1 go-live"* and go-live has happened, so the cheap-to-tune premise the assumption rested on is already false. **Neither `ASM-011` nor `OQ-035` is edited** - `OQ-035` is Deferred with a recorded resolution, and rewriting a settled answer would be a decision, not a tidy-up.

d3 - `WBS-24.1` IS ADJUDICATED NOW, PER ITEM, and moves `Review` -> `Implemented`. This takes `DEC-071` d3's stated mitigation literally: per-item adjudication was the answer to `SL-033` being one slice of eight, so each item is judged as its evidence lands rather than eight at once at slice exit. `AC-144` and the full text of `AV-222` - including what the verdict explicitly does NOT claim - were on the docket. ⚠ The parent `WBS-24` stays `Approved`; seven children remain, and the roll-up is mechanical.

d4 - `WBS-24.2` STARTS IN THE SAME SESSION. **THIS OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION** to hand off to a fresh context, which rested on the session being long and expensive and on `WBS-24.2` being a full item deserving a full context window. Second time in two interviews the operator has taken this option against that advice.
rationale:
THE FINDING THAT CHANGED A QUESTION BEFORE IT WAS ASKED, and it is the reason `LL-008` is worth its cost. The agent intended to ask whether `ASM-011` should be re-validated with the committee or re-dated. Sweeping the registers first - by keyword across acceptance criteria, ADRs, assumptions, constraints, decisions, defects, deferred work, KPIs, open questions, requirements, risks, scope changes, slices, tests and WBS items - surfaced `OQ-035`'s resolution asserting the thresholds are *configurable*, which sent the agent to the code, where `TopicAging.SlaThresholdDays` is a hardcoded switch. **Both of the options about to be offered assumed a configuration path that does not exist**, so the prepared question was the wrong question. `DEF-110` records it.

THE ABSENCE WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED. `AV-159`'s rule is that *"I searched for X and found none"* rules out X, never the family - so the search was widened until it had a working control: `IOptions<>` appears in eighteen files, so the pattern exists in this codebase and a search would have found an instance; the Topics module has exactly one options class and it is about attachments; there is no settings table. The near-miss is recorded in the row because it explains the hiding: `appsettings.json` genuinely does carry days-based thresholds, for a DIFFERENT sweep (`FR-084`), so the vocabulary answers the question truthfully about the wrong subject - `LL-015`'s shape.

THE FORM OF THE SLATE, held to `LL-023`'s own standard before `LL-023` was approved. Seventeen fields across seven records - `LL-023`, `DEF-110`, `ASM-011`, `OQ-035`, `WBS-24.1`, `AC-144`, `AV-222` - printed from the JSONL by a generator and verified byte-identical, with the verifier calibrated by injecting a single changed digit into a quoted field and confirming it was detected. **And every paragraph the agent wrote was marked as the agent's**, with the check behind each claim named, which is precisely the rule `LL-023` proposes. Applying a Proposed lesson to the interview that adjudicates it is deliberate: it let the operator see the rule working rather than only described.

WHY d4 IS RECORDED AS AN OVERRIDE. `DEC-071` d3 set the precedent that what the operator DECIDED stays separate from what the agent INFERRED, and that reasoning-against is preserved rather than harmonised away. The agent's case for handing off was context and cost; the operator's choice to continue is theirs to make and is recorded as taken against that advice, not as agreement with it.

title:
WBS-24.5 IS BUILT AS THE FULL SLICE THE ARCHITECTURE SPECIFIES: the Configuration table, its write path, authorization, an audit event on write, and an admin surface. OPERATOR OVERRIDE of the agent's narrower recommendation, 2026-08-27.

WHAT WAS PUT TO THE OPERATOR. `DW-036` describes `WBS-24.5` as *"retention CONFIGURABILITY only"*. Reading the code and then the narrative documents before writing any code showed the row was covering a subsystem: `SEC-080` names the home explicitly - *"the Configuration table (`16` section 2.15) holds retention settings for legal/compliance to set later"* - and `SEC-103` specifies it as `Key NVARCHAR` UNIQUE, `Value NVARCHAR` holding JSON, `Scope NVARCHAR`, `Guid` PK, adding that *"Retention is configurable here (no purge v1, `NFR-059`)"* and that secrets stay OUT of it. **The table does not exist**, verified with a control because the obvious grep lies: `class Configuration` matches only EF entity-type configurations under `Persistence/Configurations/`, while the control term `class Stream` resolves to a real domain entity.

⚠ THE AGENT'S EARLIER RECOMMENDATION WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE THIS DECISION, NOT BY IT. Having found no settings store, the agent had proposed appsettings-backed options with a read-only display. That would have been an architectural DIVERGENCE from `SEC-103`, and the agent said so once it read the narrative rather than only the code.

**THE DECISION: option 2 of four - the FULL slice.** Table, migration, read AND write paths, authorization, an `AuditEvent` on write, and an admin surface.

⚠⚠ THE REASONING-AGAINST IS PRESERVED, per the `DEC-071` d3 precedent, because this is an override and should not be read as agreement. The agent recommended the narrower cut - table, migration, read path and an honest read-only display - deferring the privileged WRITE surface and its audit event to a `DW-` row triggered by legal defining periods. The argument was that **the full mechanism buys nothing observable in v1**: `SEC-080` states periods are *"configurable but unset in v1"*, `OQ-DATA-004` makes the periods themselves an open question awaiting legal, and `SEC-089` places retention **enforcement in Phase 2**. So v1 ships an empty table behind a write surface for values nobody has defined, enforcing nothing. The operator accepted that cost knowingly.

WHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT TOUCH. `DEC-013` remains Approved canon - keep all records, no auto-purge in v1, retention configurable, immutable classes protected - and is reopenable only via a new ADR. **Nothing here builds or schedules a purge**, and `NFR-059`/`NFR-060`'s *no automatic purge in v1* clause binds the build: a purge job would VIOLATE the requirement, not complete it. Legal hold (`OQ-DATA-003`, `[unverified - confirm hold workflow with legal]`) stays out of scope.

CONSEQUENCES THE BUILD MUST HONOUR. `SEC-077` classifies a *"retention/immutability config change"* as a **privileged action that must be audited**, so the write path emits an `AuditEvent`. The Administration design reference draws exactly five tabs and the app implements those five, so a retention surface is a **no-reference composition** and must be flagged as one (`INV-014`, `CLAUDE.md`). Module boundaries (`ADR-0001`) apply to a cross-cutting Configuration table and the owning module is the build's first question.

TWO RULINGS, 2026-08-27, AT THE START OF `WBS-24.6`. d1: `WBS-24.4` IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented`. d2: `FR-154`'s ROLE CLAUSE IS RECONCILED TO `ADR-0027` VIA A SCOPE CHANGE.

d1 - `WBS-24.4` -> `Implemented`. The row had been withheld TWICE. The first withholding (2026-08-26) had a stated cause - `AC-147` carried an exclusion clause the definition of done forbids - and that cause is `DEF-111`, Fixed and merged at `2b0da29`, with `AC-148` carrying the corrected criterion and its own `Met` verdict. A SECOND decline followed on 2026-08-27 with NO reason recorded anywhere. The agent ASKED rather than inferring, per `LL-003`; the operator promoted the row. `WBS-24.4` is now `Implemented` and slice-scope `wbs-done` for `SL-033` names only `WBS-24`, `WBS-24.6`, `WBS-24.7` and `WBS-24.8`.

d2 - `FR-154`'s ROLE CLAUSE. `FR-154` states the audit export is *"accessible only to Auditor and Administrator"*. `ADR-0027` (Approved) decides that audit read, search, EXPORT and delete are `{Auditor, Chairman, Secretary}` with **Administrator excluded** on segregation-of-duties grounds, and it names exporting explicitly. `ADR-0027` recorded that `FR-151` and `FR-153` would carry a pointer to it; both do, as `relates_to` edges. `FR-154` carries NO such edge and no pointer - it was a Phase-2 requirement when the ADR was written and was simply missed.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN OPEN QUESTION. The ADR's decision clause already covers exporting, so the BUILD is not ambiguous and follows `ADR-0027` whichever way this ruling went. What was at stake is only whether the register goes on contradicting the code it governs. The operator chose to reconcile it rather than merely record the contradiction (`DEC-079` d2's *record it, change nothing* disposition was offered and not taken) or leave it unrecorded.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method is the transferable part. `WBS-24.6`, `DW-035` and `FR-154` all quote the same superseded clause faithfully, so every register view agrees with every other one and nothing looks wrong. It surfaced only from sweeping the ADR and decision registers before writing code - trap 32 and `LL-008` - and was then confirmed against the code, where `Policies.AuditRead` and the `App.tsx` route gate had BOTH already implemented the ADR's set. **A row can be an accurate quotation of a requirement clause that an ADR has already superseded**, which is a distinct failure mode from the five `SL-033` has produced so far and is invisible to an id-and-status pass.

TWO RULINGS, 2026-08-27, CLOSING `WBS-24.6`. d1: `WBS-24.6` IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented`. d2: `LL-025` IS APPROVED AND PINNED.

d1 - `WBS-24.6` -> `Implemented`. The audit-log export shipped as PR `#317` -> `ca75244` with all three CI workflows green. `AC-152` is `Met` (`AV-230`), evidenced against the merged commit: sixteen new API cases (the assembly moved 368 -> 392, so they are proven to have RUN by the count), three guards mutation-proven with each mutant confirmed to have compiled first, and the refusal proven by forcing it - Administrator, Member, Reviewer and Submitter all 403 against `ADR-0027`'s excluded set. `FR-154` auto-advanced to `Implemented` and `DW-035` is `Done`. The `SC-032` axe obligation is discharged and was proven to have run rather than inferred from a green job: the e2e count moved 88 -> 90, and the 88 baseline was RE-MEASURED from PR `#316`'s own run rather than quoted.

THE OPERATOR READ THE GENERATED SLATE, NOT A SUMMARY. `scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs` printed `AC-152`'s full canonical text from the JSONL, including the four things the criterion deliberately does NOT claim - no actor display-name resolution in the export format, no `C-INS-01` anomaly alert (carried as `DW-087`), the `Report.Export` composition recorded as ANALYSIS because no role discriminates it, and no `/audit/export` route because `INV-014` gives the design reference precedence over `SEC-177`'s sitemap. `LL-011` and `LL-023` are discharged mechanically here rather than remembered.

d2 - `LL-025` APPROVED AND PINNED, the operator having read the generated docket carrying its full text. The lesson: a plan row can be a FAITHFUL quotation of a clause an ADR has already superseded, and nothing mechanical can see it - the ids resolve, the statuses are right, the trace gate passes, and the registers agree with each other about a sentence a decision overruled. Where an ADR names the rows it undertook to amend, that list is the instrument: `ADR-0027` named `FR-151` and `FR-153`, both carry the edge, and `FR-154` had neither.

⚠ `handoff_emit` RUNS IN THIS SAME BATCH, and that is not ceremony. `DEF-107` records a lesson that was Approved, pinned and operator-attributed while binding NOTHING for two days, because the note every session loads is rebuilt only by `handoff_emit` and nothing compares it against the pinned set. `lessons-confirmed` cannot catch it - it counts `Proposed` rows, so it goes green the instant a lesson is approved, propagated or not.

THREE RULINGS OPENING `DW-080`, 2026-08-27. d1: PROCEED NOW, IN TWO PHASES. d2: THE PHASE-B BASE IS DECIDED LATER, WITH EVIDENCE. d3: `#318` AND `#319` ARE LEFT ALONE.

d1 - `DW-080` STARTS NOW, phase A (the `net8.0` -> `net10.0` runtime migration on the Debian base) then phase B (`DW-066`'s minimal-base move). The row's own instruction governs the split: *"land them in an order that lets you attribute a failure - runtime first on the existing Debian base, then the base move - rather than in one commit."*

⚠⚠ THE OPERATOR RULED WITH A KNOWN OVERLAP IN VIEW, AND THE ANALYSIS BEHIND IT IS RECORDED AS ANALYSIS. `DEF-108` (Open/high) is the backend job dying in the Testcontainers SQL Server path on commits that changed no backend code - four data points, no verdict - and that is the SAME job that would catch a runtime-migration regression. The agent's reading, which NO instrument has measured, is that the two present differently: `DEF-108` is a CONTAINER-STARTUP death and since `DW-084` it surfaces as a `TimeoutException` naming the container, the bound and the startup log tail, whereas a musl/ICU/native-load regression surfaces INSIDE a running test as a globalization exception, a native load failure, or wrong FREETEXT results. **If the backend job goes red, `DEC-077` d3 still binds: STOP, report the signature, do not re-run.** The ambiguity therefore costs a stop, not a wrong conclusion, and that is the cost the operator accepted.

d2 - THE PHASE-B BASE (alpine vs distroless) IS NOT CHOSEN HERE AND MUST NOT BE CHOSEN SILENTLY. `DW-080`'s row leaves the fork open and the two options fail differently: alpine is musl rather than glibc, and this application does Arabic and English culture-aware work plus SQL Server native interop, so ICU behaviour is the whole question - **verify whether the aspnet alpine image ships without ICU and what that implies for `FREETEXT` and `LCID 1025` before recommending it**; distroless avoids musl but has NO SHELL, which changes the container healthcheck and anything the entrypoint shells out to. The agent spikes both in phase B and brings a decision with MEASURED findings. `NFR-054`'s minimal-base clause was KEPT rather than relaxed (`SC-024`, the operator declining the narrowing), so this is the route to evidencing it and it deserves a recorded choice.

d3 - `#318` (nginx digest) AND `#319` (npm minor/patch group, 8 updates) ARE LEFT OPEN AND UNTOUCHED. Both appeared AFTER the `DW-078` sweep and are covered by no prior decision. **They were NOT folded in, and the reason is this row's own origin story:** `DW-080` exists because `DEC-072` d1's *"sweep everything, majors included"* was authorised over a `gh pr list` truncated at ten, so `#128` and `#134` - the oldest and largest items - were never in the description the operator approved (`PE-599`). Stretching a past *"everything"* over work nobody has seen is the exact failure that produced this row, and it is not repeated here. `DW-080`'s own trigger also requires nothing else in flight.

⚠ A STALE REPO CLAIM CORRECTED IN PASSING: `prm-next.md` said *"the only two open PRs, `#128` and `#134`"*, re-verified 2026-08-26. Measured today with no `--limit` cap there are FOUR. That is a moving queue rather than a wrong statement when written, but the sentence was live instruction and is fixed.

OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-28 (AFTER `DW-080` PHASE A MERGED): `LL-026` APPROVED AND PINNED AFTER A FALSE CLAUSE WAS CORRECTED; `LL-023` + `LL-027` MERGED INTO `LL-028`; `SL-033` IS FINISHED BEFORE PHASE B; `DEF-114` GETS ITS OWN PR; THE `LL-003` MISS IS JOURNALLED, NOT MADE A LESSON.
decision:
d1 - `LL-026` IS APPROVED AND PINNED, BUT ONLY AFTER ONE FIELD WAS CORRECTED. Its `recommendation` was written before CI adjudicated the fix and told the reader to join a `BackgroundService` with `StopAsync`. CI then proved `StopAsync` is NOT a safe join - it cancels the stopping token before awaiting, so on a loaded runner it can cancel the body before the thread pool starts it. The operator was shown the before/after of that single field and chose to correct then approve, rather than approve as written and supersede later. ⚠ The remaining six fields are byte-identical to what was read. THE CATCH MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX: approving would have made an instruction the same session had already disproven IMMUTABLE and pinned into every future startup note - inside a lesson whose own subject is tests that pass while proving nothing. It is `LL-020` exactly: the correction reached `DEF-113`, the commit message, the resume and the memory index, and missed the lesson row.

d2 - `LL-023` AND `LL-027` ARE MERGED INTO `LL-028`, WHICH IS APPROVED AND PINNED; BOTH SOURCES ARE `Superseded`. The operator selected approve-and-pin for both proposed lessons AND the merge, which combine in more than one way, so the agent did NOT guess: it drafted the merged wording, put the end-states side by side with the draft visible, and asked. The chosen shape approves the merged row WITHOUT approving `LL-027` separately first - `LL-027`'s content still binds, through `LL-028`, and no row is approved and then retired minutes later. Same shape as `LL-007` + `LL-012` into `LL-013`. The pinned set is 24 rows.

d3 - `SL-033` IS FINISHED BEFORE `DW-080` PHASE B: `WBS-24.7`, then `WBS-24.8`, then phase B. THIS RESOLVES A REAL AMBIGUITY RATHER THAN RESTATING AN ORDER. The stream order was set by `DEC-076` d3 and amended by `DEC-077` d5 and `DEC-078` d2, all reading `SL-033` -> `DW-080` alone -> `DW-079`. But `DEC-083` d1 said *"phase A ... then phase B"* while `WBS-24.7` and `WBS-24.8` were still open, and said nothing about them - silent rather than overriding. Both readings were defensible and the operator took the one that keeps the standing order intact.

d4 - `DEF-114` IS FIXED NOW, IN ITS OWN PR. One line: the forced-build image gets a per-run name so Testcontainers can never skip the build. The deciding argument was that the local backend gate has just been shown to reproduce CI exactly (461 files, 99.60%) and `DEF-114` is the single thing making that false - 65/68 locally against CI's 66/68 - so fixing it restores an instrument the next work depends on, now that Docker is running.

d5 - THE `LL-003` NON-COMPLIANCE IS RECORDED AS PROGRESS ONLY; NO NEW LESSON. The operator observed that a lesson already instructs the agent to open an interview with named options and a recommendation, and they are right: `LL-003` rule 3 says *"name the options and show what each looks like in practice"* and rule 5 says *"where an option carries a risk the operator has not seen, state it inside the option"*. This was non-compliance, not a gap in the register, so it does not earn a row in the pinned set.
rationale:
WHAT THE AGENT DID WRONG, RECORDED BECAUSE THE CORRECTION CAME FROM THE OPERATOR AND NOT FROM THE AGENT. Homework was done and a verified decision slate was published - `LL-011` and the merged `LL-028` discharged mechanically, every cited record byte-identical, the verifier calibrated on two injected faults. Then the agent STOPPED at a prose list of options instead of asking, and withheld a recommendation on the lessons on its own reading of `DEC-075` d4. `LL-003`'s first clause is *"never surface a blocker and then stand still"*. ⭐ THE SHAPE WORTH SEEING: producing the artifact FELT like discharging the obligation, because `LL-011`'s remedy is itself an artifact - so one lesson's remedy displaced another lesson's duty, and the more rigorous the artifact got, the more complete the turn felt.

A SECOND AGENT INFERENCE IS CORRECTED BY d3 AND IS RECORDED AS AN INFERENCE. Before this interview the agent had already written *"phase B is item 1"* into `prm-next.md` and pushed it. That was never the operator's ruling. It was disclosed on the slate, labelled as an inference rather than presented as settled, per `DEC-071` d3's standing separation between what the operator DECIDED and what the agent INFERRED - and d3 now overrides it, so the file is corrected rather than left standing.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-28, SIZING WBS-24.8 (DW-028, the /session presenter preview) BEFORE ANY CODE: d1 ISOLATE THE PREVIEW BEHIND THREE INDEPENDENT REFUSAL LAYERS. d2 MATERIALS ARE LISTED, NOT OPENABLE. d3 A SUCCESSFUL PREVIEW IS AUDITED. d4 THE CRITERION BINDS TO A NEW REQUIREMENT VIA A SCOPE CHANGE, NOT TO FR-159. All four followed the agent's recommendation.
decision:
d1 - ISOLATE THE PREVIEW. It gets its own SPA route guarded to Chairman and Secretary, its own API group sited OUTSIDE the guest path allowlist, and its own query carrying an AllowedRoles set that does not contain Guest. GetMySessionQuery is not touched. THE REASONING THE OPTION WAS PUT ON: the /session read path's security today IS an absence. Its own header states that there is no parameter naming a meeting, a topic or a person, so a guest cannot ask for somebody else's session because the question cannot express it - and it says in as many words that this is a stronger guarantee than checking that they did not. WBS-24.8 asks for exactly that parameter, so the item does not extend the design, it trades a structural guarantee for a conditional. Isolation keeps the guest's own handler byte-identical and puts the conditional somewhere a guest never reaches. The three layers refuse with DISTINGUISHABLE signatures - a route guard, a path-gate header, and an application-layer audit row - so a forcing test can prove WHICH layer refused rather than merely that something did, which is what makes each one independently provable rather than three restatements of one control. REJECTED: extending /session with an optional target, which is the smaller surface but leaves the ONLY refusal a branch inside the one handler a guest does reach, because the path gate already allowlists that prefix and the route guard already admits guests. ALSO REJECTED: the two-layer middle, which keeps the query separate but renders the preview as a state on /session, where the route guard cannot participate.

d2 - MATERIALS ARE LISTED, NOT OPENABLE, and the acceptance criterion says so in its own text. Names, types and sizes render; no open control. THE ARGUMENT THAT CARRIED IT IS NOT THE ARGUMENT FIRST OFFERED - see the rationale, where a false premise was measured and withdrawn BEFORE the operator ruled. The surviving argument is that a second targeted pre-signed-URL path over content scoped to another person is the largest single piece of new attack surface in this item, and the preview's purpose is to show the presenter's shell rather than to exercise it. REJECTED: full parity through a targeted materials endpoint, which is the most faithful reading of renders that person's view and of DEC-037 clause 3, but would ship the product's FIRST non-guest attachment download as a side effect of a preview feature - which is DW-088's own first activation trigger, and would leave the committee able to open a file through a preview of somebody else's view but not through the topic that owns it. ALSO REJECTED: rendering the open control disabled in the manner the topic detail screen already uses, which is visually faithful at zero cost but propagates a knowingly-inert affordance onto a brand-new surface.

d3 - A SUCCESSFUL PREVIEW IS AUDITED, not only a refused one. The event names the caller as subject and the targeted meeting and topic as data, and the test asserts it as a ROW rather than as a log line. THE COST WAS STATED BEFORE THE RULING AND ACCEPTED: this becomes only the SECOND audited successful read in the entire product. The first and only other is the audit-log export, which control C-AUDIT-08 forced to be a server-side action for exactly this reason; a sweep of every audit emit site found no query or Get feature folder emitting anything at all. So this sets a precedent for every future read gate rather than following one. The reasoning FOR: one principal looking through another person's scoped view is a governance act, and WBS-24.5 established that a privileged action is an audited action - the difference being that WBS-24.5's was a write. REJECTED: refusals only, which matches every other read in the system and matches the permission and role matrix, whose audit clause is written about DENIED attempts - but which would leave the one action this item exists to make possible with no trace at all, the mirror image of DEF-056.

d4 - THE NEW CRITERIA BIND TO A NEW REQUIREMENT, ADDED BY A SCOPE CHANGE. A sweep of the requirement register found the concept of previewing in ZERO of 227 rows, against a control of seven rows matching presenter. FR-159 is about INVITING a guest presenter with an expiring window and is already Implemented, so binding a preview criterion to it would make a settled requirement silently carry a clause nobody wrote into it - which is LL-025's exact shape, the failure WBS-24.6 paid for three days earlier. REJECTED: binding to FR-159 on the strength of the lineage, which is real - OQ-074 was raised and resolved inside that requirement's orbit - but lineage is not statement. ALSO REJECTED: binding to FR-022 or FR-023, which are closer in subject matter but are both written from the invite and assignment direction rather than the preview direction, and would trade one imperfect fit for another without adding a row.
rationale:
THE FORM. Every question carried its load-bearing text VERBATIM rather than by identifier - the source comments from GetMySession.cs, DEC-037's clause 3 and clause 4, WBS-24.8's own warning, FR-159's statement, and the permission and role matrix's audit clause - so no ruling rests on a record the operator could not read (LL-011, which a previous interview was refused for lacking). Every sweep ran with a control in the opposite direction so a zero is a result rather than a silence (LL-013): zero preview requirements against seven presenter matches; zero covering deferred-work rows against 27 topic matches; zero query-handler audit emits against sixteen emit sites overall.

THE SWEEP RAN BEFORE THE INTERVIEW, NOT AFTER, AND IT CHANGED A QUESTION. The agent's plan message had asserted that Chairman and Secretary could already open a presenter's materials from the topic screen, and therefore that withholding an open control in the preview cost them nothing. THAT WAS FALSE. Measured: there are exactly TWO production callers of the pre-signed-URL method in the whole solution - meeting recordings, and the topic reader's material lookup, which is reached only through the caller-scoped /session materials handler. The SPA's topic API has an upload helper and no download call at all, and the topic detail screen renders its per-attachment download button hardcoded disabled with a coming-soon title. So the ONLY principal who can open a topic attachment anywhere in the product is a guest presenter, and only for the single topic on their own agenda slot. The entire argument the agent had offered for d2 was therefore built on an unmeasured premise - LL-028 firing exactly as written, on a sentence that read as rigorous precisely because it was unnecessary. It was caught and withdrawn before the operator ruled, and d2 was carried on a different argument.

THE FINDING WAS FILED BEFORE THE QUESTION WAS ASKED, SO THE FORK WAS NOT PREJUDGED. DW-088 records the inert download affordance and its inverted capability gradient. Filing it first was deliberate: whichever way d2 went, the row is correct and unchanged - a deferred-work row is a record, not a schedule - and holding it back until after the ruling would have made the operator's answer determine whether a measured gap got written down.

ALL FOUR RULINGS FOLLOWED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, and each recommendation was disclosed as the agent's inference rather than as a reading of the plan (the DEC-071 d3 separation). Two of them - d1 and d3 - are the STRICTER option in a place where the looser one is defensible, which is consistent with how this operator has ruled four times on a control that went red.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT ASKED, so the silence is not read as oversight. The target's identity (meeting plus topic rather than a member id) is an engineering call and was decided by the agent, with reasoning: it names exactly one agenda item, where a member id would re-run the which-meeting heuristic that only makes sense for a caller. Whether the axe obligation gets its own criterion or rides inside the feature criterion is likewise the agent's call and was decided as its own, so the clause cannot go invisible inside a larger verdict. DEF-108 was not raised - settled twice, strictest option taken, no new occurrence. The two open dependency pull requests were not raised - DEC-083 d3 already left them alone and nothing has changed.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (SECOND ROUND, ON `SL-033`'s CLOSE): THE SLICE STAYS OPEN UNTIL `DEF-108` IS CHASED. This RESOLVES the clause `DEC-087` d4 deliberately left open, and it reverses that round's first answer once the collision with `DEC-077` d1 was put in front of the operator.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (THIRD ROUND, AFTER THE SL-033 REVIEW): d1 DEF-108 GETS A CHECKABLE END CONDITION WRITTEN INTO THE ROW. d2 SL-034 IS CREATED WITH WBS ROWS FOR DW-080 PHASE B AND DW-079. d3 DEF-116's UNENFORCED CONVENTION IS CARRIED AS DW-089. d4 DW-088 STAYS OPEN AS FILED. The row's trigger fires on a SECOND occurrence or on any change to how reviews are produced, and deliberately does NOT fire on a clean review, since a safeguard doing its job is containment rather than discovery.

title: OPERATOR DECISION, 2026-08-29, ON `DW-080` PHASE B AFTER THE SPIKE: d1 THE BASE IS `aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra`. d2 THE HEALTHCHECK BECOMES A TINY .NET PROBE INVOKED WITHOUT A SHELL. Both followed the agent's recommendation, and both were taken against MEASURED findings rather than documentation, as `DEC-083` d2 required.
decision:
d1 - THE api AND worker IMAGES MOVE TO `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra`. Measured against the four alternatives: 162 MB against Debian's 229 (-29%); medium CVEs 26 -> 4 and low 13 -> 7, with NO highs, where BOTH alpine variants carry two highs that neither Debian nor chiseled has; glibc rather than musl, which removes the native-interop risk `DW-066` and `DW-080` both name around `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`; and ICU 74.2, the SAME version Debian ships, which is why the same published binary produced BYTE-IDENTICAL Arabic output on both. It satisfies `NFR-054`'s 'equivalent distroless' clause, which `SC-024` kept rather than relaxed.

REJECTED: `10.0-alpine-extra`, and the reason is the finding the spike exists to have produced. It is 3 MB smaller and keeps a shell, so the healthcheck would have survived untouched - but it ships ICU 78.1 against Debian's 74.2, and CLDR changed `ar-SA`'s default calendar in that range, so the SAME binary renders a Hijri date on Debian and a Gregorian one on alpine-extra. No exception, no log line, Arabic only. It also carries the two high-severity CVEs and reintroduces musl. The convenience was real; the two costs are precisely the ones this project weighs heaviest.

ALSO REJECTED: plain `chiseled` or `alpine` with no ICU, despite being smallest and cleanest on CVEs. They are defensible ONLY on the measured fact that ACMP's API does no culture-aware work today, and they do not fail loudly if that ever changes. ALSO REJECTED: staying on Debian, which would leave `NFR-054`'s clause unsatisfied and reverse `SC-024`.

d2 - THE api HEALTHCHECK BECOMES A SMALL .NET PROBE INVOKED AS `CMD` WITH NO SHELL. Chiseled ships no shell and no package manager, and the current check is `CMD-SHELL` running `curl -f http://localhost:8080/readyz`, so it cannot survive the base change in any form. The probe is published beside the application and invoked through the `dotnet` host already present in the image, and it keeps probing `/readyz` exactly as today.

WHY NOT THE CHEAPER ROUTES, recorded because the cheapest one is the trap. Copying a static `curl` in would be the smallest diff and zero new code, but it puts a native binary back into an image whose entire purpose is minimal surface, and it then needs tracking and patching like any other dependency. Moving the check to the compose layer as a TCP probe needs nothing at all - and rebuilds `DEF-079` exactly, where a healthcheck that could only fail if the process stopped answering TCP was itself the defect, on a `/healthz` endpoint mapped with a predicate that evaluated NO checks. `/readyz` reaches SQL Server, Hangfire and object storage, and that reach is the whole value of the check.
rationale:
THE SPIKE FALSIFIED THREE CLAIMS THE PACKAGE ITSELF CARRIED, and the decision rests on the corrected picture rather than the recorded one.

FIRST, and it inverts the risk. `prm-next.md` and `DW-080` both said a naive minimal-base move would not degrade Arabic but would THROW at runtime after compiling and unit-testing perfectly. Measured by publishing ONE binary and running it unchanged on all five bases: a no-ICU image does NOT abort at startup. The app starts, exits 0, and silently enters globalization-invariant mode, throwing only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED. And ACMP's API touches none - all 10 `CultureInfo` usages in `src` are `InvariantCulture`, and `RequestLocalization`, `SupportedCultures`, `IStringLocalizer`, `Accept-Language`, `new CultureInfo` and `.resx` return ZERO across 693 `.cs` files. So the predicted loud failure would not have happened; what would have shipped is a container in which the first server-side culture-aware code anyone ever writes throws in Arabic, with nothing failing in between. The trap is armed and invisible rather than loud, which is worse than the row predicted, not better.

SECOND, the risk was framed as musl versus glibc and the risk that actually bites is the ICU VERSION, which is orthogonal to it and would have applied to a glibc option too.

THIRD, `DEC-083` d2 asked what a no-ICU base implies for `FREETEXT` and `LCID 1025`. Measured: nothing. Every `LCID 1025` reference is an EF migration creating a full-text index with `LANGUAGE 1025`, executed inside the `sqlserver-fts` container - an image `NFR-054` excludes from the size cap and this change does not touch at all. Arabic word-breaking cannot be affected by the api base, and the spike's attention went to the culture surface that CAN be.

AN INSTRUMENT FAILURE IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY DECIDED THIS WRONGLY. The probe printed 'invariant-mode: off' on the very images where the runtime WAS in invariant mode: `AppContext.TryGetSwitch` reports the explicit SWITCH, and the runtime falls back to invariant when ICU is absent WITHOUT setting it. Reading the flag would have reported every base as healthy. The behavioural probe - attempt a culture and see what happens - is what produced the true answer. Separately, a PowerShell tar probe reported NO ICU for `chiseled-extra` whose own behaviour proved otherwise; the bash form measured ICU 74.2, and nothing was reported until the two agreed, because a verifier that disagrees with observed behaviour is the verifier being wrong.

⚠ WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN AND MUST BE PROVEN BY THE IMPLEMENTATION: the spike measured the BASE, not the application on it. `DW-080` requires the full e2e leg and Arabic `FREETEXT` verified end to end before any of this is believed, and that obligation is untouched by these rulings.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (FOURTH ROUND, OPENING SL-034): d1 THE SLATE GENERATOR IS EXTENDED TO RENDER A DELIBERATELY CRITERION-LESS ITEM. d2 WBS-25.2's PACK IS A NEW DOCUMENT DERIVED FROM DOC-067, WHOSE STALENESS IS RECORDED AS A DEFECT. d3 IT LIVES UNDER tamheed-package/docs/. All three were put after a keyword sweep of the narrative and decision registers, not before.
decision:
d1 - WBS-25.1's REVIEW IS UNBLOCKED BY EXTENDING THE INSTRUMENT, NOT BY WORKING AROUND IT. scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs aborts FATAL on WBS-25.1 because that row's title names no acceptance criterion. The refusal was RUN, not predicted. WBS-25.1 is criterion-less deliberately: DW-090 records that NFR-054's own verification method names a CI check (docker image inspect; assert size <= 500 MB; base image layer verified) that does not exist in any of the three workflow files, so an AC written today would either claim a CI-verified property nothing verifies, or rest on a one-off local measurement by the agent that made the change. The generator therefore gets a criterion-less arm: it renders the item's own completion record, its DW- row, the deciding DEC-, and an explicit block stating that no criterion exists and quoting the recorded reason - so a reader who has never opened this package can still adjudicate. It goes branch -> PR -> green CI -> squash-merge, because scripts/** is carved out of the direct-to-main allowance by DEC-077 d2. A hand-built slate was offered and DECLINED: this generator IS how LL-011 is discharged, so rendering the review by hand is the exact harm DEF-116 was filed to prevent. Filed as DEF-117.

d2 - WBS-25.2 PRODUCES A NEW ASVS-CHAPTER-ORGANIZED PACK DERIVED FROM DOC-067, AND DOC-067's STALENESS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN INHERITED. DOC-067 ('Security Controls Audit - ACMP (OWASP ASVS 5.0 L2)', Approved, docs/validation/security-controls-audit.md) already holds the control -> status -> code path -> test -> threat -> residual ledger that DW-079 lists as the pack's raw material, and DW-079 never mentions it. Measured: the document carries ZERO ASVS chapter references - not one V-numbered clause; 'ASVS' appears only in its title - so it is organized by ACMP's own C-AUTH-*/C-WEB-*/C-CRYPTO-* taxonomy and by P16 batch, and the chapter mapping that IS DW-079's deliverable is entirely absent. It was last touched 2026-07-17 and at least one row is now measurably false: C-AUTHZ-04 reads 'Deferred-feature - No Confidentiality/Restricted field exists in code', while SL-030 shipped exactly that and Confidentiality now resolves across ten or more source files. The new pack reuses DOC-067's verified control/code/test rows only after re-verifying each against current code, and adds what post-dates it. Refreshing DOC-067 in place was offered and DECLINED because it means editing docs/, which AGENTS.md freezes read-only; building fresh and ignoring DOC-067 was offered and DECLINED because it discards weeks of verified mapping and leaves two documents disagreeing. Filed as DEF-118.

d3 - THE NEW DOCUMENT LIVES UNDER tamheed-package/docs/ AND IS REGISTERED AS A NEW DOC- NARRATIVE-DOCUMENT ROW. Measured: all 69 existing narrative-document rows point into docs/, and the only post-freeze commits to that tree are the two lines in docs/README.md that record the freeze itself - so nothing established where post-freeze prose goes, and this ruling establishes it. A new top-level validation/ was offered and DECLINED (a second prose tree outside the package); docs/validation/ alongside DOC-067 was offered and DECLINED (it erodes the read-only rule that stops the archive being read as current). The package tree is already path-ignored by all three workflows, so the write goes direct to main - and that is not a convenience but a constraint: ci.yml, e2e.yml and security.yml ALL path-ignore '**/*.md' and 'docs/**', so a markdown-only PR fires no workflow at all and would hang forever against branch protection's nine required checks, which is strictly worse than the package-only-PR case DEF-105 records.
rationale:
WHY d1 IS AN INSTRUMENT FIX AND NOT A ONE-OFF. The generator's zero-criterion arm carries a comment arguing it is deliberate rather than leftover strictness: 'an item sitting at Review naming no criterion is genuinely unreviewable, and rendering it would hand the operator a page with nothing to adjudicate'. That is a claim about EVERY criterion-less item, and it is false about this one. WBS-25.1 has a full completion record - a merged PR, a measured size and CVE delta, a deciding decision row, two residual deferred-work rows - and the ONLY thing absent is a criterion, whose absence is itself recorded and reviewable. The timing is the sharp part and is measured, not recalled: the zero-arm comment landed at 03:57 on 2026-08-29 in commit 3f93ba66, and WBS-25.1 was created criterion-less at Review at 06:35 the same morning in commit 20f0b61c - two hours and thirty-eight minutes later, by the same day's work. An unmeasured universal falsified within three hours by the project's own next merge is this package's signature failure mode, and DEF-116's own text says an item the generator cannot render is one whose review would have to be hand-built, which LL-011 forbids. This is DEF-116's family, third instance: exactly one, then one-or-more, now zero-with-a-recorded-reason.

WHY d2 REJECTED BOTH SIMPLER ANSWERS. DW-079's row reads as a from-scratch build and never names DOC-067, so the honest sizing was only reachable by sweeping the narrative register by KEYWORD rather than by identifier - LL-008 and LL-025 firing together on the first item of the slice. Refreshing in place is the cheapest move and it is the one that quietly breaks a standing rule: docs/ is a frozen read-only archive superseded 2026-07-22, and a single justified exception is how a freeze stops meaning anything. Building fresh is the most defensible-sounding move and it is wasteful in a way that also carries risk: DOC-067's rows name specific code paths and specific tests, and discarding them means re-deriving mappings that were verified when they were written, while leaving an Approved package row asserting a control set that disagrees with the new pack. Deriving-and-re-verifying is the only option that both preserves the verified work and forces every inherited row to be checked against current code before it is repeated - which is what caught C-AUTHZ-04 in the first place.

WHY THE STALENESS IS A DEFECT ROW AND NOT A FOOTNOTE. DOC-067 is Approved and asserts, of a control the product now has, that no field for it exists in code. Left unrecorded, that assertion survives in an Approved package row while a new document says the opposite, and the next reader gets to choose - the shape prm-next.md records as handing the reader the choice with the stale half wearing the detail. DEF-118 makes the disagreement visible instead of resolving it silently, and it deliberately does NOT repair the archive file, because repairing it would be the docs/ edit d3 declined.

WHAT WAS NOT DECIDED, stated so nobody reads more into this than was ruled. WBS-25.1's VERDICT was not taken - it cannot be, until the generator can render its slate, and taking it early is precisely the shortcut d1 refused. NFR-018 is untouched and stays Approved with no acceptance criterion; DW-079's own text and trap 16c both forbid writing one from this pack, because acs-met counts by retired_in and an AC ahead of an external assessor's report holds package readiness false permanently. DW-090's missing CI check was offered as a third route to unblocking d1 and was DECLINED as turning a review into a build; it stays Open and unscheduled.

title: OPERATOR VERDICT, 2026-08-29: `WBS-25.1` (`DW-080` PHASE B) IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented`. Taken against a GENERATED slate for the first time on a criterion-less item - the instrument that makes such a review possible was built in the same session, because the review could not otherwise be held without hand-building the page `LL-011` forbids.
decision:
`WBS-25.1` MOVES FROM `Review` TO `Implemented`. The item shipped as PR #325 -> `1d7cb04b` with ten checks green including the e2e leg the row itself demanded: the api and worker images move to `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra`, measured at 326 MB -> 258 MB (-21%) with application CVEs 75 -> 11 (-85%) and zero criticals on either side. `DEC-090` d1 chose the base and d2 replaced the shell healthcheck with `Acmp.HealthProbe`.

WHAT THE PROMOTION CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, stated because this item has no criterion to bound it. It claims the WORK: the minimal-base move is built, measured and merged. It does NOT claim `NFR-054`. That requirement stays `Approved` and carries no acceptance criterion, because its own verification method names a CI check - `docker image inspect`, assert size <= 500 MB, base image layer verified - that exists in none of the three workflow files, so any criterion written today would either claim a CI-verified property nothing verifies or rest on a one-off local measurement by the agent who made the change. `DW-090` is the honest instrument for that gap and stays Open.

TWO RESIDUALS STAY OPEN AND NEITHER IS SWEPT INTO THE VERDICT. `DW-090` - no CI check asserts image size or base layer, and a size check ALONE would have passed on Debian at 326 MB, reporting compliance with a minimal-base clause while sitting on the base that clause excludes. `DW-091` - both api dependents use `service_started` rather than `service_healthy`, so nothing consumes the new healthcheck's verdict; that is `DEF-078`/`DEF-079`'s shape a third time, with a compose comment asserting the opposite.

WITHHOLDING UNTIL `DW-090`'s CHECK EXISTED WAS OFFERED AND DECLINED, on the ground that it converts a verdict into a build. Naming a different concern was offered and declined.
rationale:
WHY THE ABSENCE OF A CRITERION DID NOT BLOCK THE PROMOTION. The definition of done here is criterion-driven, so a criterion-less item at `Review` looks like a gap by construction. It is not one: the criterion is absent because writing one would be dishonest, and the REASON is recorded in `DW-090` and adjudicable on its own terms. The slate quoted that reason verbatim beside the completion record, so the operator ruled on the actual question - is this work done and honestly bounded - rather than on the absence of a field.

WHY THE SPIKE'S OWN FINDINGS STRENGTHEN THE VERDICT RATHER THAN COMPLICATE IT. The row predicted that a no-ICU base would THROW at runtime because ACMP creates `ar-SA` and performs LCID 1025 FREETEXT. The spike falsified that: a no-ICU base does not throw, it starts, exits 0 and silently enters invariant mode, throwing only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED - and this API touches none (all ten `CultureInfo` uses are `InvariantCulture`; `RequestLocalization`, `IStringLocalizer`, `.resx` and `new CultureInfo` are zero across 693 files). So plain chiseled would have looked perfectly healthy while arming a trap, which is WORSE than the loud failure the row predicted. The real discriminator turned out to be the ICU VERSION rather than musl - alpine-extra ships ICU 78.1 against chiseled-extra's 74.2, and CLDR moved `ar-SA`'s default calendar between them, so the same binary renders a Hijri date on one and a Gregorian one on the other with no exception and no log line, in Arabic only. LCID 1025 was separately measured to be a SQL Server concern executed inside `sqlserver-fts`, an image `NFR-054` excludes and this change never touches. A decision that corrected its own premise with measurements is better evidenced than one that merely confirmed it.

THE STANDING CONSEQUENCE, WHICH OUTLIVES THIS VERDICT: the `-extra` suffix is LOAD-BEARING. A digest bump that silently dropped it would pass every existing gate, because the failure is a silently wrong Arabic calendar rather than an exception. Until `DW-090`'s base-layer assertion exists, nothing mechanical catches that.

WHY THE REVIEW COULD NOT HAVE BEEN HELD AN HOUR EARLIER. `scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs` refused to render any item naming no acceptance criterion, and that generator IS how `LL-011` is discharged - so this verdict would have required a hand-built page, which is exactly what the operator once refused an interview over. `DEF-117` fixed it; `DEF-119`, a second defect that made `WBS-24.5` unrenderable for a different reason, was found by the regression case written to prove the untouched path still worked. Both merged as #326 -> `964ab01a` before this verdict was sought.
source_span: Operator verdict 2026-08-29 on WBS-25.1; slice-review slate generated from tamheed-package/data at 964ab01a; DEC-090; DW-090; DW-091

title: OPERATOR VERDICT, 2026-08-29: `WBS-25.2` (`DW-079`, THE ASVS L2 EVIDENCE PACK) IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented`. `SL-034`'s BUILD IS COMPLETE. The second criterion-less verdict in one session, and the second taken against a generated slate.
decision:
`WBS-25.2` MOVES FROM `Review` TO `Implemented`. It shipped as PR #327 -> `58b900b0` with ten checks green, producing `DOC-070` at `tamheed-package/docs/asvs-l2-evidence-pack.md` - the first narrative document in this package to live outside the frozen `docs/` archive, per `DEC-091` d3.

WHAT THE PROMOTION CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims THE PACK: it exists, it is organized by ASVS chapter, its structural claims are mechanically derived, and its cited paths are gated in CI. It does NOT claim `NFR-018`, which stays `Approved` with no acceptance criterion - and here that is the row's OWN standing prohibition rather than a discovered gap: Level 2 conformance is established by an external assessor, and an acceptance criterion written from this pack would hold package readiness false permanently because verdicts are counted by retirement rather than lifecycle status. `DW-079` stays the honest instrument for the distance between the pack and the requirement.

FOUR GAPS FOUND WHILE RE-VERIFYING, ALL FILED AND ALL CARRIED IN THE PACK RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. `DW-093` - `C-AUTH-05`'s SoD-4 clause has no hard guard, measured as `SoD-1`/`2`/`3`/`5` appearing 11/10/13/11 times in `src` against `SoD-4` appearing ZERO, with the four non-zero siblings as the control proving the sweep had a subject; its only prior record was a *"verify in a later batch"* in the frozen archive and no register row knew. `DW-092` - `C-INS-01`'s Restricted-topic-access alert, the sibling of `DW-087`'s export half, where one sentence justified two exclusions and only one was ever corrected. `DEF-118` - `DOC-067` is stale and its title claims an ASVS mapping its body does not contain. And the measured plaintext-hop set: at least four internal endpoints, where `DOC-067` names two and `DEF-100`/`DW-074` name two DIFFERENT ones, so neither record is wrong and neither is complete.

WITHHOLDING TO READ THE PACK END TO END FIRST WAS OFFERED AND DECLINED. Naming a different concern was offered and declined.
rationale:
WHY THE PACK'S REFUSALS ARE THE REASON TO PROMOTE IT RATHER THAN A LIMITATION OF IT. The single most likely failure for this deliverable was to assemble it from the existing catalogue and inherit that catalogue's conclusion - `docs/domain/security-controls.md` section 20 ends *"L2 is met across all applicable chapters"*, which is precisely the self-assertion of conformance `DW-079` forbids, and it is one copy-paste away from turning an orientation document into a false claim handed to a paid third party. The pack declines it explicitly and says why. A document that states plainly what it is not is worth more to an assessor than one that overstates what it is.

WHY THE SIZING MOVED TWICE AND WHY THAT IS THE METHOD WORKING. `DW-079` reads as a from-scratch build. Sweeping the narrative register by KEYWORD rather than by identifier found `DOC-067`, an Approved document titled for ASVS that the row never mentions - so the item was BIGGER than written, because that document is stale and its staleness would otherwise have been inherited silently. Then reading the control catalogue found section 20's full V1-V17 map - so it was SMALLER than it had just become, because the chapter mapping did not need inventing. Both corrections came from the sweep and neither from the row, which is `LL-008` and `LL-025` firing together on a single item.

WHY ITS STRUCTURAL CLAIMS CAN BE TRUSTED WITHOUT RE-READING THEM. The chapter list, titles and level counts come from the authoritative OWASP machine-readable release rather than from recollection: 17 chapters, 345 requirements, L1 70 / L2 183 / L3 92, and because ASVS levels are cumulative the pack states that *Level 2* means the 253 requirements at L1+L2 rather than the 183 tagged L2 - a distinction easy to get silently wrong. The `[unverified titles]` marker the catalogue had carried is discharged: 17 claimed, 17 official, 0 mismatched, with the comparison CALIBRATED FIRST by injecting ASVS 4.0's *"Malicious Code"* in place of V5 and confirming the checker reported it, because a clean result from an uncalibrated checker proves nothing. The control-to-chapter map was extracted from TWO independent keys across all 72 controls - the per-control ASVS column and each section heading's own V-suffix - and 41 of the 72 disagree between them, so a single key would have silently dropped mappings (`LL-009`).

WHAT THE NEW CI GATE IS AND IS NOT. `scripts/check-asvs-pack-paths.mjs` asserts every repository path the pack cites still exists, and fails closed below twelve citations because a checker that finds nothing and exits 0 reports a clean result over an empty set (trap 31, `DEF-078`'s shape). It asserts EXISTENCE, never sufficiency - whether the code at a path implements the control it is cited for is the assessment itself. It is positioned deliberately: `ci.yml` path-ignores both markdown and `tamheed-package`, so editing the pack never runs it, and it fires when SOURCE moves, which is how the pack actually goes stale. It was PROVEN to have run in the `compose` job by reading the run log, with a control term confirming the grep had a subject - not inferred from a green job.
