title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (FIFTH ROUND, THE SL-034 POST-CLOSE DISPOSITION): SIX DEFERRED-WORK ROWS ARE ACTIVATED - EVERY ONE AGAINST THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION TO CARRY - AND THEY BECOME SL-035, SECURITY FIRST. A NEW REQUIREMENT IS CREATED FOR SEGREGATION OF DUTIES BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILT. FR-035 STAYS Implemented. DEF-108 STAYS Open.
decision:
d1 - DW-093 IS ACTIVATED: THE SoD-4 STRENGTH QUESTION IS SETTLED FIRST, THEN IT IS BUILT. OVERRIDE - the agent recommended carrying it Open on the grounds that neither trigger clause had fired and the ASVS pack already discloses the gap. Measured: C-AUTH-05 specifies SoD-1..SoD-5 as hard authorization checks, P1, ASVS V8, and across src/**/*.cs the identifiers SoD-1, SoD-2, SoD-3 and SoD-5 appear 11, 10, 13 and 11 times while SoD-4 appears ZERO. Its only prior record was a 'Partial - verify in a later batch' in the frozen archive dated 2026-07-17; no later batch did, and no register row knew.

d2 - DW-090 AND DW-091 ARE BOTH ACTIVATED, INCLUDING THE service_healthy SWITCH. OVERRIDE - the agent recommended activating DW-090 alone and carrying DW-091's semantic change, on the grounds that /readyz reaches SQL Server, Hangfire and object storage and a strict start-up ordering could turn a slow cold boot into a failed stack. The operator took the whole change. DW-090 also unblocks NFR-054, which cannot record Met until a CI check asserts image size AND base layer - and a size check ALONE would have passed on Debian at 326 MB, reporting compliance with a minimal-base clause from the base that clause excludes.

d3 - DW-092 AND DW-087 ARE ACTIVATED TOGETHER AS ONE UNIT. OVERRIDE - the agent recommended carrying both because anomaly detection needs a baseline and neither endpoint has usage history, so any threshold set today is a guess dressed as a control. The operator's reasoning for taking them together rather than folding them into DW-058 is that they are two signals of ONE control, C-INS-01, and splitting them is exactly how one half got corrected and the other did not.

d4 - DW-086 IS ACTIVATED. OVERRIDE - the agent recommended carrying it, since its trigger is a product ask nobody has made and FR-035's purpose clause is satisfied by the per-meeting count. ⛔ THE ROW'S OWN PROHIBITION SURVIVES ACTIVATION AND IS NOT SOFTENED BY IT: do NOT fan useMeetingDetail across the visible month. That is the N+1 shape DEF-104 records. The answer is a lightweight per-meeting agenda projection on the Meetings side.

d5 - ALL SIX BECOME ONE SLICE, SL-035, ORDERED SECURITY FIRST. Activation alone does not schedule: six Activated rows with no WBS- row are invisible to wbs-done, to slice and phase readiness, and missing G-TRACE's wbs-item-or-slice leg - DEF-087's shape, a rule that cannot fail rather than one that passes, and the reason DEC-089 d2 created SL-034. REJECTED: three slices by kind, and two slices splitting security from hygiene. The order within the slice is security (SoD-4, then the two C-INS-01 alerts), then deployment/CI, then the calendar projection.

d6 - A NEW REQUIREMENT IS CREATED FOR SEGREGATION OF DUTIES BEFORE SoD-4 IS BUILT. Measured before the question was put: a keyword sweep of all 228 requirements for segregation, SoD, recorder and conflict-of-interest returns three hits and NONE of them is a segregation-of-duties requirement. C-AUTH-05 is a control in the security catalogue with no requirement row at all, so the work would satisfy nothing traceable. This is WBS-23.4's situation exactly, where the pre-build sweep found no requirement covering triage reclassification and DEC-070 + SC-031 created FR-164 before the build could be recorded. REJECTED: building against the control catalogue alone, and widening an existing authorization requirement.

d7 - FR-035 STAYS Implemented; DW-086 IS A REFINEMENT BEYOND IT, NOT AN UNMET CLAUSE. The requirement reads 'showing topics by their scheduled meeting date, so that I can see how topics are spread across upcoming meetings', and AC-145 covers a per-meeting count in the grid plus titles on selection while stating the titles-in-grid exclusion explicitly rather than quietly covering less. The purpose clause is the discriminator and it is met. REJECTED: reopening FR-035, which would reverse an operator verdict already given on AC-145; and creating a separate requirement for titles-in-grid. ⚠ CONSEQUENCE, recorded so nobody looks for one later: DW-086's work advances NO requirement and needs NO acceptance criterion against FR-035.

d8 - DEF-108 STAYS Open, AND SL-033 STAYS OPEN WITH IT. DEC-089 d1's third clause - the operator explicitly converts, waives, or accepts it as environmental - was available and was NOT taken. Nothing has changed since that ruling: no diagnosis, and no recurrence carrying a log that names a cause. REJECTED: accepting it as environmental to return readiness to ready:TRUE, and converting it to deferred work, the latter having been offered and declined once already.
rationale:
WHY EVERY RECOMMENDATION WAS OVERRIDDEN, AND WHY THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. The agent recommended CARRY on all four disposition questions and the operator activated all six rows. That is the DEC-067 shape - twelve demand-triggered rows activated against the same advice - and the rows record it as an override, not as agreement. v1 is materially larger than it was an hour ago. The reasoning-against is preserved in each clause above so that a later session reading these rows does not mistake the outcome for a consensus, per the DEC-071 d3 precedent.

WHY THE SWEEP RAN BEFORE THE INTERVIEW AND WHAT IT CHANGED. LL-005's trap is that the NFR-023 question went to the operator BEFORE its sweep and the sweep would have changed the question. Here the pre-interview sweep changed two questions materially and produced d6 and d7, neither of which existed when the interview was planned: that SoD has no requirement at all, and that FR-035's own words claim more than AC-145 verified. Both are the kind of finding no id-and-status pass can surface, because in each case every identifier resolves and every status is correct.

WHY THE SLATE WAS GENERATED RATHER THAN WRITTEN. LL-011 is pinned and the operator once refused an interview because the artifact cited records by identifier alone. scripts/gen-dw-disposition-slate.mjs prints every field verbatim from data/deferred_work.jsonl; all twelve quoted fields across the six rows were then verified byte-identical against the store, with a calibration confirming the verifier discriminates. Nothing on the page was re-typed, so LL-001's untrusted-transport risk is absent by construction rather than mitigated.

⚠ A PROXY WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED WHILE BUILDING THAT GENERATOR, AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING. The obvious way to auto-select rows needing disposition is 'every Open row that no decision names', since a decision naming a row is the only evidence in this store that a human considered it. Run against this register it returns THIRTY-FIVE rows - and thirty-four of them were dispositioned on 2026-08-20 by an interview that confirmed every then-open row in BULK and therefore named none of them individually. The proxy does not measure what it appears to (LL-006). The generator now refuses to guess and demands explicit ids.

⚠ WHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT DO. It does not schedule the release close-out, which was not put: activating six rows is not the moment to close v1 out. It does not touch NFR-018, NFR-054 or NFR-046, all of which stay Approved - d2 and d6 make two of them evidenceable rather than evidenced. And it does not create acceptance criteria: an AC written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c), so each row's criterion is written in the batch that produces its evidence.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (SIXTH ROUND, THE WBS-26.1 STRENGTH INTERVIEW): SoD-4's RECORDER CLAUSE IS WARN-AND-AUDIT, ITS COI CLAUSE STAYS PHASE 2 UNDER FR-076, SoD-5 IS RECORDED AS A HARD REFUSAL, AND DEF-108 STAYS OPEN UNCHANGED ON ITS THIRD OCCURRENCE. ALL FOUR RULINGS MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION - THE FIRST INTERVIEW IN THIS PROJECT WHERE NONE WAS OVERRIDDEN, WHICH IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE OVERRIDE PATTERN IS OTHERWISE THE NORM AND ITS ABSENCE IS ITSELF INFORMATION.
decision:
d1 - SoD-4's FIRST CLAUSE (decision recorder is not the sole owner or presenter) IS ENFORCED AS WARN-AND-AUDIT, NOT AS A HARD REFUSAL. Recording is ALLOWED; the overlap is flagged on the decision and a distinct audit event is emitted, exactly as SoD-2 does for a minutes approver who is the sole author. The basis is NFR-064's own text rather than the agent's inference: that requirement states in terms that a hard recorder-is-not-the-owner rule *could block legitimate minute-taking in a committee of twenty where roles overlap by necessity; a warn-and-audit may be the correct answer*, and that the requirement demands the answer be decided and recorded, not that it be strict. RecordDecision's own header confirms the shape of the risk - *the Secretary (or Chairman) drafts a decision against a topic* is the ordinary path, so a hard guard would refuse a Secretary who also owns the topic. REJECTED: a hard refusal matching SoD-1/SoD-3, and recording SoD-4 as deliberately unenforced in v1 (which would have reversed DEC-094 d1's *settled first, then built*).

d2 - SoD-4's SECOND CLAUSE (COI exclusion) IS COVERED BY FR-076 AND STAYS IN PHASE 2. WBS-26.1 therefore covers the RECORDER HALF ONLY. THE SWEEP CHANGED THIS QUESTION AND IT IS LL-005 PAYING AGAIN: FR-076 already specifies the feature AND specifies its strength softly - *a voter may declare a conflict; the declaration is recorded without automatically excluding the voter (exclusion is a chairman decision)* - at priority S, mvp=0, Deferred, Phase 2, with DW-004 (trigger *Phase 2*, v1 handling *honor system, noted in MoM*) and WBS-9.7 already scheduling it under PH-2. ADR-0010's consequences additionally name *conflict-of-interest recusals are expressible*, and a self-declared voluntary recusal already ships. So building a COI EXCLUSION in WBS-26.1 would have contradicted FR-076's own words, which forbid automatic exclusion, and pulled Phase-2 scope into v1 without a scope change. ⚠ THE JUDGEMENT THIS RESTS ON WAS PUT TO THE OPERATOR EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN ASSUMED: FR-076 is COI per VOTE per voter while SoD-4's clause sits in a DECISION-RECORDING context, so treating FR-076 as the mechanism SoD-4 names is a judgement and not a lookup. REJECTED: filing SoD-4's COI as a distinct gap with its own DW- row, and pulling FR-076 into v1 via a scope change.

d3 - SoD-5's STRENGTH IS RECORDED AS A HARD REFUSAL, AND NFR-064 IS NOT AMENDED. SoD-5 is enforced structurally - Administrator is simply never listed in a committee-content capability's role list, so a Deny is the ABSENCE of a grant and no SoD predicate ever runs - but the RUNTIME ANSWER to an Administrator reaching committee content is a 403. *Structural* describes the implementation, not the strength, and NFR-064's binary (hard refusal or warn-and-audit) is satisfied without widening. REJECTED: adding *structural* as a third category, which would have required a scope change against an Approved requirement.

d4 - THE FIVE STRENGTHS ARE HEREBY RECORDED, WHICH IS THE CLAUSE OF NFR-064 THAT NOTHING ELSE SATISFIES. SoD-1 (action verifier is not the owner or assignee): HARD REFUSAL - SegregationOfDuties.CanVerifyAction, denied attempt audited then ForbiddenAccessException. SoD-2 (minutes approver is not the sole author): WARN-AND-AUDIT - approval allowed, isSoleAuthor persisted, a distinct Meetings.MinutesApprovedBySoleAuthor event emitted. SoD-3 (vote cast, count and chairman override distinct, co-attested tally): HARD REFUSAL - SegregationOfDuties.HasIndependentCoAttestation, denied attempt audited then ForbiddenAccessException. SoD-4 (decision recorder is not the sole owner or presenter): WARN-AND-AUDIT per d1, currently UNBUILT. SoD-5 (Administrator excluded from all committee-content authority): HARD REFUSAL per d3, enforced by non-grant. ⚠ THIS IS THE RECORDED STATEMENT NFR-064's verification detail DEMANDS AND IT IS NOT THE EVIDENCE - that requirement also demands, per rule, a test that FORCES the refusal or, for a warn-and-audit rule, asserts the warning AND the resulting AuditEvent as a ROW. NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS WRITTEN BY THIS DECISION: a criterion ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c), so NFR-064's criteria land in the batch that produces the evidence.

d5 - DEF-108 STAYS OPEN, UNCHANGED, ON ITS THIRD OCCURRENCE, AND ITS END CONDITION IS NOT AMENDED. THE EVIDENCE PUT TO THE OPERATOR WAS NEW AND DID NOT EXIST AT DEC-094 d8 - CI run 33255612333 on commit b246888a (PR #329) failed the backend job with no backend code in the commit (measured: one .mjs file, no .cs, .csproj, Dockerfile or .sql), and for the first time SQL Server CRASHED and captured a core dump whose stack runs sqlpal.dll to lsasrv.dll to lsass.exe, the SAME LSA subsystem as occurrence 2's *Failed to load LSA: 0xc0070102*, adding Last errno 11, *Resource temporarily unavailable* (EAGAIN), on a 4-processor runner. THE RULING RESTS ON WHAT THAT EVIDENCE IS NOT: EAGAIN during LSA start-up is CONSISTENT WITH resource exhaustion and that is a hypothesis, since nothing isolated a variable, so end-condition clause (1) - *the cause identified with evidence* - is not met. Clause (2)'s presentation half is also unmet: the container crashed rather than hung, so DW-084's bound never expired and the log was carried by Testcontainers' own ContainerNotRunningException. REJECTED: scheduling a controlled diagnosis as a new WBS row in SL-035; treating clause (2) as met in substance and chasing the row; and clause (3), accepting it as environmental. ⚠ THE RED WAS NOT RE-RUN, per DEC-077 d3.

d6 - THE WORDING DEFECT IN CLAUSE (2) IS RECORDED AS A FINDING RATHER THAN REPAIRED. Clause (2) requires the recurrence to fire *under DW-084/DW-085's bounded presentation*, which names a MECHANISM where the property it means is *a captured log names a cause*. That is DW-087's exact shape - a trigger naming an item rather than a property, so the row cannot see its own condition met from another direction - repeating inside the very clause DEC-089 added to escape it. The finding is filed as a lesson (Proposed, for a later interview against its full text); the clause itself is left alone, because amending it would have chased the row and d5 declined to.
rationale:
WHY EVERY RULING MATCHED THE RECOMMENDATION, AND WHY THAT IS WORTH RECORDING AT ALL. Five of the last six interviews here overrode the agent on at least one clause, and DEC-094 overrode it on all six activations. This one overrode nothing. The absence of an override is recorded deliberately, because a reader who knows only the override pattern would otherwise assume one and go looking for the preserved reasoning-against. There is none to find: the options were put with the agent's recommendation stated and separated per DEC-071 d3, and the operator took each.

WHY THE SWEEP RAN BEFORE THE INTERVIEW, AND WHAT IT CHANGED. LL-005's trap is that the NFR-023 question reached the operator BEFORE its sweep and the sweep would have changed the question; DEC-094's own rationale records the same mechanism paying twice. Here it paid again and harder. A keyword sweep of every register - JSON-parsed per line, never a regex over a JSONL row, with control terms proving the sweep had subjects - returned FR-076, DW-004, WBS-9.7 and ADR-0010 against conflict-of-interest keys. Without it, d2 would not have been asked at all, and WBS-26.1 would have been built with a COI exclusion that FR-076's own words forbid.

⚠ AND THE SWEEP CONTRADICTED THE ROW THAT SCHEDULED THE WORK. DW-093 states that sweeping the deferred-work, defect, open-question, requirement, decision and ADR registers for SoD-4 *or the COI rule* returns ZERO rows. It returns three. That claim is corrected in DW-093 itself by SC-039 rather than only here, because a correction applied to one artifact and not its sibling leaves the surviving copy as the one the next session reads. ⚠ NOTHING HERE DIAGNOSES WHY THE ORIGINAL SWEEP RETURNED ZERO: its instrument was never recorded, so any account of the cause would be a guess, and the discrepancy is reported without one.

⚠ A SECOND RECONCILIATION, NOTED SO THE RECORD IS STRAIGHT AND NOT TO REOPEN ANYTHING. DEC-094 d6's *a keyword sweep of all 228 requirements returns three hits and NONE of them is a segregation-of-duties requirement* reconciles exactly with this session's sweep - FR-076, FR-085, FR-154 - so the count is right. FR-085 does name SoD-1 explicitly in its own text. That does not disturb NFR-064, whose value is the five-rule scope and the strength clause, and d6 is not reopened.

WHY THE SLATE WAS GENERATED RATHER THAN WRITTEN, AND WHAT THE GUARANTEE COVERS. LL-011 is pinned and the operator once refused an interview because the artifact cited records by identifier alone. This question spanned a requirement, an ADR, two deferred-work rows, two WBS rows, a decision and ten source-file excerpts, and no existing generator covers that span - the three that exist are each welded to one register, which is DEF-116's shape. A general one was built (scripts/gen-record-slate.mjs, PR #329), and the slate's eighteen blocks were each re-read from their own source and confirmed byte-identical after rendering, with the comparison calibrated first against a deliberately corrupted checker that it detected. ⚠ THE GUARANTEE IS PROVENANCE, NOT CORRECTNESS, AND THE CONNECTIVE PROSE CARRIES NEITHER - LL-023, and the TWENTY-SEVENTH reached a decision slate through exactly that seam, so the framing section is rendered inside a band that says so.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-29 (SEVENTH ROUND, THE WBS-26.1 BUILD-SHAPE INTERVIEW): THE SoD-4 GUARD COVERS OWNER **AND** PRESENTER, WBS-26.1 CARRIES NFR-064's EVIDENCE FOR ALL FIVE RULES, PR #329's BRANCH IS UPDATED AND ALLOWED TO RE-RUN, AND LL-033 IS APPROVED AND PINNED. THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP AGAIN CHANGED THE QUESTIONS - IT FOUND THAT SoD-2's WARN-AND-AUDIT TEST ASSERTS A MOCK CALL AND NOT AN AUDIT ROW, SO THE REQUIREMENT'S BAR IS UNMET EVEN BY THE RULES THAT SHIPPED.
decision:
d1 - PR #329's BRANCH IS UPDATED AGAINST `main` AND CI IS ALLOWED TO RE-RUN. `main` has moved twice since the branch and strict branch protection REQUIRES a branch be up to date before merging, so updating is a mandatory step and a fresh run is its consequence rather than its purpose. ⚠ THE PRACTICAL EFFECT WAS STATED TO THE OPERATOR PLAINLY RATHER THAN HIDDEN: it is also, in effect, a retry, which is exactly why the agent did not take it alone. `DEC-077` d3's stop rule asked that a red from `SearchProvidersFtsTests` be treated as real and INVESTIGATED rather than re-run to see whether it passes; that investigation happened, is recorded as `DEF-108`'s third occurrence with its crash dump and subsystem link, and the row stays Open. REJECTED: leaving the PR untouched indefinitely (which would strand the generator off `main`, leaving trap 27's *if you build an instrument worth trusting once, commit it* partly undischarged); an operator bypass merge; and closing the PR, which would discard the instrument that made the `WBS-26.1` slate possible and would force the next cross-register interview to be hand-built - `DEF-116`'s harm.

d2 - THE SoD-4 GUARD COVERS THE TOPIC OWNER **AND** THE AGENDA PRESENTER. This is what `C-AUTH-05` says (*decision recorder != sole owner/presenter*) and what `NFR-064`'s own statement repeats, so it is the baseline rather than an expansion: an acceptance criterion covering the owner alone would quietly cover less than its criterion, which is the failure the definition of done exists to prevent. ⚠ THE COST WAS PUT TO THE OPERATOR BEFORE THE RULING, MEASURED: `Topic.OwnerId` exists but `ITopicReader`'s `TopicSummary` exposes id, key and title only, so that seam widens; `AgendaItem.PresenterUserId` exists and NONE of the three Meetings cross-module seams (`IMeetingQuorumSource`, `IMeetingWebexWriter`, `IWebexMeetingProvisioner`) surfaces it, so a NEW seam is needed - both under `ADR-0001`, which forbids a module reading another module's tables. ⚠ `Decision.MeetingId` IS NULLABLE, so a decision with no meeting has no presenter and that half of the check simply does not apply; that is a behaviour to implement deliberately and to state in the criterion, not an edge case to discover. REJECTED: owner-only in v1 with the presenter half deferred, which would have narrowed `NFR-064` below its own wording and required a scope change plus a deferred-work row.

d3 - `WBS-26.1` CARRIES `NFR-064`'s EVIDENCE FOR ALL FIVE RULES, NOT ONLY SoD-4's. The requirement demands, PER RULE, a test that FORCES the refusal or - for a rule recorded as warn-and-audit - asserts the warning AND the resulting AuditEvent AS A ROW. THE SWEEP FOUND THAT BAR IS NOT MET TODAY EVEN BY THE RULES THAT SHIPPED: `MinutesHandlerTests`' SoD-2 case asserts `audit.Received(1).EmitEnrichedAsync(...)`, a MOCK INTERACTION, where the requirement asks for a row - and SoD-2 is precisely the pattern SoD-4 must follow, so the precedent was short of the standard the new work is held to. The upgrade is reuse rather than invention: `RefusalAuditTests` already reads `audit.AuditEvents` through the real web-application factory. One acceptance criterion then covers all five and `NFR-064` can reach `Implemented`. ⚠ AN HONEST CAVEAT WAS RECORDED WITH THE OPTION AND IS REPEATED HERE: only SoD-2 was measured as falling short; SoD-1, SoD-3 and SoD-5 were NOT fully audited against the bar, so the size of the upgrade is not yet known and may grow. If it grows beyond the item, the honest instrument is a scope change and a sibling row, never a criterion that covers less than it says. REJECTED: building SoD-4 alone and deferring the four-rule audit to a deferred-work row (smaller, but leaves `NFR-064` open); and splitting the audit into a separate sibling `WBS-` row immediately.

d4 - `LL-033` IS APPROVED AND PINNED. The operator read the exact statement rather than selecting a finding - `DEC-075` d4's rule, that selecting a finding is not approving a sentence they have not read. ⚠ `handoff_emit` RUNS IN THE SAME BATCH AND THE REBUILT NOTE IS COMMITTED: `DEF-107` is this project's record of a lesson that was Approved, pinned and operator-attributed while binding NOTHING for two days, because only `handoff_emit` rebuilds the note every session loads and `lessons-confirmed` goes green the instant a row is approved, propagated or not.
rationale:
WHAT THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP CHANGED THIS TIME, BECAUSE IT HAS NOW ALTERED THREE CONSECUTIVE INTERVIEWS AND THAT IS THE POINT OF `LL-005`. Reading the actual SoD tests rather than counting them turned d3 from a scheduling question into a finding: every one of the four built rules HAS a test naming it, so an identifier census would have reported full coverage, and the requirement's real bar - a forced refusal, or a warn-and-audit's AuditEvent asserted as a ROW - is not met by SoD-2's mock assertion. That is trap 33's shape exactly, *a count of the enforcing mechanism is not a measure of the property*, found by reading the predicate instead of the count.

WHY d2 IS RECORDED AS A BASELINE RATHER THAN AN EXPANSION. `NFR-064`'s statement names *SoD-4 decision recorder is not the sole owner or presenter*. Building the owner half alone would not have been a smaller build of the same thing - it would have been an acceptance criterion asserting less than the requirement it is bound to, which `SL-033`'s programme repeatedly found to be the expensive failure. The cost of the presenter half is a new cross-module seam, and the cost was measured and put in front of the operator before the ruling rather than discovered during the build.

WHY d1 WAS ASKED AT ALL RATHER THAN TAKEN. Updating a branch against `main` is a required step under strict protection, so on a narrow reading it needs nobody's permission. But its side effect is a fresh CI run on a tree whose last run was the red that `DEC-077` d3 turns into a mandatory stop, and a rule that can be satisfied on a technicality is a rule an agent should not satisfy on a technicality. The distinction was stated in the option itself, not buried in it.

⚠ WHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT DO. It writes NO acceptance criterion - the strength is decided and the scope is settled, but the evidence does not exist, and a criterion ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently (trap 16c). It does not touch `DEF-108`, which stays Open per `DEC-095` d5, so readiness stays `ready:FALSE` by decision. It does not reorder `SL-035`, which is `DEC-094` d5's.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-30 (EIGHTH ROUND): DEF-108 IS ACCEPTED AS ENVIRONMENTAL UNDER ITS OWN CLAUSE (3) AND CLOSES AS Won't-fix, AND PR #330's FAILED JOB IS RE-RUN - WHICH IS AN EXPLICIT OVERRIDE OF DEC-077 d3 AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. THE FOURTH OCCURRENCE IS WHAT CHANGED THE ANSWER: THE BACKEND CODE WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO A TREE THAT HAD PASSED NINETY MINUTES EARLIER.
decision:
d1 - DEF-108 IS ACCEPTED AS ENVIRONMENTAL AND CLOSES AS `Won't-fix`, UNDER CLAUSE (3) OF THE END CONDITION `DEC-089` d1 GAVE IT. That clause reads: *the operator converts, waives, or accepts it as environmental with the reasoning recorded, which is not chasing but is a legitimate end and is named here so the hold cannot become permanent by omission.* It was offered at `DEC-094` d8 and NOT taken, and offered again at `DEC-095` d5 and NOT taken. It is taken now because the EVIDENCE CHANGED, not because the question was asked a third time.

WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF CLAIM FROM THE ONE DECLINED TWICE. Occurrence 4 fired on commit `083848db`, which is `3ed9440b` plus a merge of `main` carrying package rows only. Measured: `git diff 3ed9440b 083848db -- src/ tests/` returns EMPTY. `3ed9440b`'s CI run had been FULLY GREEN ninety minutes earlier - frontend, backend and compose - with `Acmp.Integration.Tests` at 69 passed / 2 skipped / 71 and this very test passing. **Identical backend code, identical container image, identical runner specification, opposite verdicts.** Every earlier occurrence supported only the weaker statement *a commit that did not change backend code*; this one is the SAME backend code, which is as close to a controlled comparison as CI can produce. ⚠ THE PRIOR RULINGS WERE ABOUT A HYPOTHESISED CAUSE (`EAGAIN` implying resource exhaustion) AND THIS ONE IS ABOUT OUR CODE'S INNOCENCE - a different claim, and the reason declining twice and accepting now is consistent rather than a reversal.

THE SIGNATURE ALSO REPRODUCES FRAME FOR FRAME, INCLUDING OFFSETS. Occurrences 3 and 4 both report `Reason 0x00000002`, `Parameters [0] 0x10010`, `Last errno 11` / *Resource temporarily unavailable*, the same build stamp, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, 4 processors and 16766414848 bytes, with the stack running `sqlpal.dll` five times then `lsasrv.dll` at `+0xAB7F9`, `+0x620B2`, `+0x613E9` then `lsass.exe` at `+0x2551`, `+0x2494`, `+0x4A74`. Occurrence 2's *[AppLoader] Failed to load LSA: 0xc0070102* is the same subsystem in a different presentation. So the fault sits at ONE deterministic site in SQL Server's LSA start-up path.

⚠ WHAT IS STILL NOT CLAIMED, AND THE CLOSURE DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT. The TRIGGER is not diagnosed. A resource exhaustion failing at a single allocation site would produce exactly this constant stack every time, so an identical trace is CONSISTENT with the `EAGAIN` reading without confirming it, and `LL-029` is the standing warning that reproduction proves sufficiency and never causation. No variable was isolated. Clause (1) - *the cause identified with evidence* - is therefore NOT satisfied, and this closure is explicitly clause (3) and not clause (1).

d2 - PR #330's FAILED BACKEND JOB IS RE-RUN. ⛔⛔ THIS IS AN EXPLICIT OVERRIDE OF `DEC-077` d3, WHICH SAYS WITHOUT QUALIFICATION THAT *a red from `SearchProvidersFtsTests` is treated as REAL - stop and investigate. Re-running to see whether it passes is NOT the response.* The operator has upheld that rule strictly on every previous occasion, and it is being set aside here deliberately rather than reinterpreted quietly.

WHY IT IS COHERENT RATHER THAN MERELY PERMITTED. d3's purpose is that the ONE test exercising `FREETEXT` against real SQL Server must never be lost silently to a re-run, so a red must be investigated first. It WAS investigated: four occurrences are recorded with run ids, commits, symptoms and two full crash dumps, and d1 above dispositions the cause. Re-running AFTER a disposition is a different act from re-running INSTEAD of investigating. ⚠ THAT DISTINCTION IS THE AGENT'S FRAMING AND NOT A CLAUSE OF `DEC-077`; the rule as written is unconditional, so this is recorded as an override on its face and a later session must not read d3 as containing an exception it does not contain.

d3 - THE BLOCKED STATE THAT FORCED THE QUESTION IS RECORDED, so a later reader understands why a re-run was even on the table. PR #330's FIRST run was fully green. It could not merge only because `main` had moved and strict protection requires an up-to-date branch; the update itself triggered the second run, which failed on `DEF-108` alone. The branch was then already current, so no further update could change anything, and with re-running forbidden the PR could not resolve itself by any action available to the agent. **A rule that cannot be satisfied and cannot be escaped is a deadlock, and breaking one belongs to the operator.** REJECTED: an administrator merge bypassing the required checks, and leaving the PR blocked until a diagnosis that clause (1) may never receive.
rationale:
WHY THIS IS NOT THE THIRD ASKING OF A SETTLED QUESTION, WHICH IS THE OBJECTION IT MOST INVITES. `LL-002` requires the interview to run every time and forbids banking an earlier answer; the mirror risk is re-litigating something the operator has closed. What protects this round is that the EVIDENCE is new and is of a different type. `DEC-094` d8 and `DEC-095` d5 were both asked against occurrences whose strongest statement was *no backend code changed in this commit* - a claim about a diff. Occurrence 4 supports *the backend code did not change at all between a pass and a failure* - a claim about two runs of one tree. The agent recommended AGAINST clause (3) on occurrence 3 and FOR it here, and the reasoning-against from that round stands unretracted in `DEC-095` d5.

WHAT CLOSING THIS ROW ACTUALLY MOVES, stated plainly because it is the first time in weeks. `DEF-108` was the ONLY blocking failure in package-scope `readiness_check` - `DEC-077` d1 carried it Open at high severity precisely so that nothing could be declared done while it stood, and that consequence was accepted deliberately. Closing it removes that hold. It does NOT close `SL-033`, which `DEC-088` keeps open, and it does not by itself make anything else done; it means the blocking rule no longer names a row.

⚠ THE STANDING RULE `DEC-077` d3 PROTECTS IS NOT REPEALED BY d2 AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SUCH. *A backend integration failure is not called flaky on the strength of one more green* still binds. What was accepted here is a disposition resting on four recorded occurrences and two crash dumps, not a green. If `SearchProvidersFtsTests` reddens again, it is a NEW finding to investigate on its own evidence - `DEF-108` being closed as environmental is not a precedent for waving the next one through, and a fresh session must file a new defect rather than appending to a closed row.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-30 (NINTH ROUND): `WBS-26.1` IS `Implemented`, `SL-033` CLOSES NOW THAT ITS ONLY HOLD HAS EXPIRED, `WBS-26.2` GETS A REQUIREMENT BEFORE IT IS BUILT BECAUSE THE REGISTER COVERS IT NOWHERE, AND `LL-034` IS APPROVED AND PINNED. THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP PRODUCED THE THIRD CLAUSE AND IT IS `DEC-094` d6's SITUATION REPEATING EXACTLY.
decision:
d1 - `WBS-26.1` IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented`. The operator's verdict, taken against the generated slate (`tamheed-package/slice-review-slate.html`) rather than a summary, per `LL-011`. ⚠ THE AGENT DELIBERATELY DID NOT RECOMMEND ON THIS CLAUSE, and the abstention is recorded because it is not an oversight: this was the agent's own work being graded, which is the `C7` *graded party grading itself* case that `gate_run`'s `audit_evidence` split exists to surface. The evidence was presented and the judgement was left whole. What it rests on: SoD-4 mutation-proven with the mutant CONFIRMED TO COMPILE, the audit event asserted as a ROW through the real factory with the owner and presenter legs proven separately, SoD-2 upgraded from a mock assertion to a row, and the coverage gate at 468 files / 99.63% / zero files under 95%.

d2 - `SL-033` IS CLOSED AS `Implemented`. `DEC-088` held it open on ONE condition and one only - *it stays open until `DEF-108`'s cause is settled* - and `DEC-097` d1 settled it under clause (3). Every blocking rule now passes: `acs-met`, `wbs-done`, `defects-closed`. ⚠ THE REASON FOR CLOSING IS THAT THE HOLD EXPIRED ON ITS OWN TERMS, NOT THAT THE SLICE LOOKS FINISHED - it has looked finished since `WBS-24.8` merged, and `DEC-088` reversed its own first answer once the collision with `DEC-077` d1 was put in front of the operator. Leaving it open now would be a hold with no stated reason, which is precisely the failure `DEC-089`'s end condition was written to prevent for `DEF-108` itself: a hold that becomes permanent by omission. ⚠ `DEF-109` stays open at medium, carried deliberately, and is NOT a reason to keep the slice open - the advisory `defects-minor` naming it is the control working.

d3 - `WBS-26.2` GETS A NEW REQUIREMENT, `NFR-065`, BEFORE ANY OF IT IS BUILT. THE SWEEP FOUND THE GAP AND IT IS `DEC-094` d6's SITUATION REPEATING: `WBS-26.2`'s own title binds it to `NFR-046`, and that requirement's statement names FOUR OPERATIONAL ALERTS - application error rate above 5/min, Hangfire failed jobs above 3 in 10 min, health-check failure on 3 consecutive, and audit-log write failure - **none of which is either of C-INS-01's anomaly signals.** Measured across every register with separator-tolerant keys, `anomaly` returns **ZERO requirements**. So the work would have satisfied nothing traceable and `G-TRACE`'s requirement leg would have had nothing to point at - `WBS-23.4`'s situation, where `DEC-070` + `SC-031` created `FR-164` before the build could be recorded, and `WBS-26.1`'s, where `DEC-094` d6 + `SC-038` created `NFR-064`.

REJECTED, AND THE REASONING IS KEPT because the rejected option is the one that looks cheapest: WIDENING `NFR-046` to cover the two signals. `NFR-046` is about OPERATIONAL HEALTH in Seq with numeric thresholds already fixed and a 60-second firing target; C-INS-01 is INSIDER-THREAT detection with no baseline at all. Folding them would make one requirement mean two things, and `NFR-046`'s 60-second target would then bind an anomaly rule that cannot honour it. ALSO REJECTED: re-scoping `WBS-26.2` to detection-only with alerting left to the ops group, and deferring the question until the item starts - the latter differs from SoD-4's deferred strength question because that one was about HOW to build, while this is about whether anything in the register is satisfied by building it at all, which shapes the acceptance criterion rather than the code.

d4 - `LL-034` IS APPROVED AND PINNED. The operator read the exact statement rather than selecting a finding (`DEC-075` d4). ⚠ `handoff_emit` RUNS IN THE SAME BATCH and the rebuilt note is committed - `DEF-107` is the record of a lesson Approved, pinned and operator-attributed while binding NOTHING for two days, because only `handoff_emit` rebuilds the note every session loads.
rationale:
WHY THE SWEEP KEEPS EARNING ITS PLACE, NOW FOUR INTERVIEWS RUNNING. `LL-005`'s trap is that a question reaches the operator before the sweep that would have changed it. Here the sweep changed d3 from a scheduling item into a finding: `WBS-26.2`'s title already NAMES `NFR-046`, so an identifier check resolves cleanly and a status check passes - the requirement exists and is `Approved`. Only READING the requirement's statement shows it covers four operational alerts and neither anomaly signal. That is `LL-025` exactly: a work row that cites its requirement accurately can still be wrong, and nothing mechanical can see it.

⚠ AND THE SWEEP ITSELF WAS RUN UNDER `LL-034`'s SIBLING, `LL-033`, WHICH WAS APPROVED HOURS EARLIER. The keys were written separator-tolerant rather than picking one spelling, which is that lesson's own remedy - and the reason the register was searched for the CONCEPT rather than for a token that happened to be in mind.

WHAT `NFR-065` MUST NOT BE, AND WHY ITS SECOND CLAUSE IS PART OF THE REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. Both `DW-087` and `DW-092` say the same thing in their own words: anomaly detection needs a baseline, neither endpoint has usage history, and a threshold chosen today is a guess dressed as a control. A requirement that said only *anomaly detection exists* would be satisfied by any invented number and would therefore be unfalsifiable - the class of requirement this register has repeatedly found to be undecidable rather than merely unverified. `NFR-064`'s strength clause is the precedent: where the ambiguity is the hard part, the requirement demands that the answer be DECIDED AND RECORDED rather than demanding a particular answer.

⚠ WHAT `NFR-065` DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER: C-INS-01's *optional dual-control* half. `OQ-025` - *Require dual-control or audit + alert for high-sensitivity operations?* - is `Deferred`, and this decision does not disturb it. The requirement covers the alert half only, and says so in its own text so a later session does not read the two as one.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-30 (TENTH ROUND, THE `WBS-26.2` BUILD-SHAPE INTERVIEW): READ-AUDITING IS ADDED FOR `Restricted` TOPICS BECAUSE NOTHING RECORDS THEM AT ALL, DETECTION LIVES IN THE APP WITH SEQ NOTIFYING, AND EVERY THRESHOLD IS PROVISIONAL AND CONFIGURABLE. THE SWEEP FOUND THAT `DW-092`'s CENTRAL PREMISE IS FALSE.
decision:
d1 - READ-AUDITING IS ADDED FOR `Restricted` TOPICS. ⚠ THE SWEEP FOUND `DW-092`'s PREMISE IS FALSE. That row states *"SL-030's authorization decisions already emit audit rows, so the data such an alert would consume accumulates from now."* Measured 2026-08-30: **18 write features in Topics use `IAuditSink` and ZERO read features do**, and the entire `Abac/` folder - `ConfidentialityRequirement`, `AbacProviders`, `StreamScopeRequirement` - contains no audit emission whatever. `Topics.TopicRestricted` exists but is the event for MARKING a topic restricted, not for accessing one. **So nothing anywhere records who read which `Restricted` topic, and signal 2b was undetectable by ANY mechanism - Seq or app - until something records it.**

THE PRECEDENT IS IN-REPO AND THE BUILD FOLLOWS IT: `Meetings.RecordingAccessed` audits SUCCESSFUL recording access, emitting the subject id only and deliberately never the pre-signed URL. ⚠ THE COST WAS PUT TO THE OPERATOR RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the audit log is hash-chained and inherently serialising (`ADR-0009`, `ADR-0030`), and `DW-053` names throughput as the shape that surprises you. The volume argument is from the CONSTRAINTS - a single committee of at most twenty users reading a subset of topics - and is an argument, not a measurement. REJECTED: scoping signal 2 to recordings only, which delivers half of what C-INS-01 names; and not adding it at all, which would be a second deliberate gap on a P1 control whose original exclusion is already withdrawn.

d2 - THE APPLICATION DETECTS; SEQ NOTIFIES. C-INS-01 says *anomaly alerting VIA SEQ*, while `NFR-065` - drafted by the agent and approved yesterday - says *the APPLICATION shall detect ... emitting a distinct, queryable record when a signal fires*. ⚠ THE AGENT FLAGGED THAT THE NARROWING WAS ITS OWN AND THAT THE TWO MIGHT NOT BE THE SAME THING. The ruling reads them coherently rather than choosing between them: `C-AUDIT-05` already specifies that privileged actions *emit high-importance audit events FEEDING `C-INS-01`*, so the app owns DETECTION and Seq owns NOTIFICATION. ✅ `NFR-065` therefore stands as written and needs no scope change. ⚠ THE DECIDING ARGUMENT WAS TESTABILITY: a Seq alert rule is configuration no gate can see, which is this project's recurring failure - a control nothing verifies (`DEF-078`'s healthcheck evaluating zero checks, `DEF-079`'s allowlist, `DW-091`'s unconsumed healthcheck). App-side detection is versioned, mutation-provable and does not wait on a running stack. REJECTED: Seq owning the rule, which would need an `SC-` against `NFR-065` and would put the requirement in the ops group blocked on a running stack; and additionally committing an unapplied Seq rule specification, on the ground that a specification nobody applies is a document rather than a control.

d3 - EVERY THRESHOLD IS RECORDED AS *PROVISIONAL PENDING A BASELINE* AND ITS VALUE IS CONFIGURABLE. Both `DW-087` and `DW-092` say a threshold chosen today is a guess dressed as a control, and neither endpoint has usage history. `NFR-065`'s second clause exists exactly so that *provisional* is a legitimate answer - the requirement demands the basis be STATED, never that it be derived. ⚠ THE VALUES GO IN THE `ConfigurationSetting` STORE `WBS-24.5` BUILT, NOT IN A HARDCODED SWITCH, AND `DEF-110` IS WHY: that open defect records the topic urgency SLA thresholds as a hardcoded 3/7/21 while `ASM-011` and `OQ-035`'s recorded resolution both promise the committee will adjust them via configuration - so the remediation path does not exist. Filing a second instance of that shape knowingly, on a fresh control, was rejected.
rationale:
THE SWEEP CHANGED THE QUESTION FOR THE FIFTH INTERVIEW RUNNING, AND THIS TIME IT INVALIDATED A PREMISE THE OPERATOR HAD ALREADY RULED ON. `DEC-094` d3 activated `DW-087` and `DW-092` together partly on the reasoning that the data both alerts would consume was already accumulating. For the export half that is TRUE and was verified - `audit.exported` records `Actor`, `RowCount` and every filter as received. For the Restricted-topic half it is FALSE. Had the build started from the row's own words, signal 2b would have been implemented against a data source that does not exist, and the failure would have presented as an alert that never fires - which is `DEF-078`'s shape, a control that runs and cannot fail usefully.

⚠ WHY THIS IS NOT `DW-092` BEING CARELESS. The row's claim is true of the half it was written about most directly and true in spirit of SL-030's work - ABAC decisions ARE made on every read; they simply are not RECORDED. The distinction between a decision being taken and a decision being audited is invisible unless you look for an `IAuditSink` in the authorization path, which is what the sweep did. It is `LL-006`'s family: the row is a proxy for the code, and the proxy was wrong in a way no identifier or status check could reveal.

WHAT THE AGENT RECOMMENDED AND WHERE IT OWNED A NARROWING OF ITS OWN. All three rulings matched the recommendation. On d2 the agent additionally disclosed that `NFR-065`'s *the application shall detect* was its own drafting choice from the previous round and might be narrower than `C-INS-01` intends - rather than letting a requirement it wrote silently determine the architecture. The ruling vindicated the wording, but the disclosure was made before the answer was known.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-31 (ELEVENTH ROUND, THE `DEF-121` RED-MAIN INTERVIEW): THE ROW STAYS `Open`/high AND IS INVESTIGATED, THE FAILED BACKEND JOB IS RE-RUN, AND `WBS-26.3` HOLDS UNTIL `main` IS GREEN. TWO OF THE FOUR RULINGS OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, AND THE TWO OVERRIDES ARE COHERENT WITH EACH OTHER RATHER THAN IN TENSION: THE RE-RUN IS WHAT MAKES THE HOLD DISCHARGEABLE.
decision:
d1 - `DEF-121` STAYS `Open` AT HIGH SEVERITY AND IS INVESTIGATED. Package-scope `readiness_check` therefore stays `ready:FALSE` on this row alone, and that is accepted deliberately - `DEC-077` d1's disposition for exactly this class, taken again on its own evidence rather than by precedent. MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION. The reasoning: this is ONE occurrence carrying a NEW signature (`Reason 0x00000006`, errno 2 / ENOENT, an `AppLoader`-reported LOAD failure with no `lsasrv.dll` or `lsass.exe` frame) where `DEF-108`'s closure rested on FOUR recorded occurrences and TWO full crash dumps, and that closure's own text forbids being cited as precedent for waving the next one through. ⚠ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST THIS RULING WAS PUT TO THE OPERATOR AND IS PRESERVED SO IT IS NOT LOST: the evidence that finally settled `DEF-108` - a tree byte-identical to one that passed, with opposite verdicts - arrived HERE on occurrence ONE rather than occurrence four, so an immediate environmental disposition was genuinely available. It was not taken. REJECTED: accept as environmental now; give it a checkable end condition before dispositioning; convert to a `DW-` row.

d2 - THE FAILED BACKEND JOB ON RUN `33297623382` IS RE-RUN, TO RESTORE A GREEN CI VERDICT ON `main`. ⛔⛔ **THIS IS THE SECOND EXPLICIT OVERRIDE OF `DEC-077` d3 IN TWO DAYS AND IS RECORDED AS AN OVERRIDE ON ITS FACE, NOT AS AN EXCEPTION.** `DEC-077` d3 as written is unconditional - *a red from `SearchProvidersFtsTests` is treated as REAL: stop and investigate; re-running to see whether it passes is NOT the response* - and it still contains no exception, for a dispositioned cause or for any other reason. `DEC-097` d2 was the first override; this is the second. OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, and the reasoning-against is preserved because it was evidential rather than procedural: **the green ALREADY EXISTS on byte-identical code** - PR `#331`'s head `6e8d4b96` ran `Acmp.Integration.Tests` at 69 passed / 2 skipped / 71 two minutes before the merge run failed, and `git diff 6e8d4b96 c273294c -- src/ tests/` is EMPTY - so a re-run can produce no fact the register does not already hold, and the agent argued the override would be spent on nothing. The operator ruled otherwise. ⚠⚠ **A GREEN RE-RUN DISCHARGES NOTHING AND MUST NOT BE READ AS DOING SO.** `DEF-121` stays `Open`/high under d1 regardless of the re-run's outcome, and the standing rule it inherits from `DEF-108` is untouched: *a backend integration failure is not called flaky on the strength of one more green.* The re-run's purpose is repository hygiene - a green branch verdict on `main` - and it is not evidence about the defect. REJECTED: do not re-run; re-run and amend `DEC-077` d3 to make the exception explicit.

d3 - `WBS-26.3` DOES NOT START WHILE `main`'s LATEST CI RUN IS RED. `AGENTS.md`'s *no phase starts with red CI* is read strictly and applied at the SLICE-ITEM boundary, not only at a phase gate. OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, which was to start it: the agent argued that the rule is a phase-gate rule, that we are mid-slice rather than at a phase boundary, that the tree is proven sound by the PR-head green on byte-identical code, and that `WBS-26.3` goes via PR anyway so its own PR run is the gate that actually adjudicates it. That reasoning is preserved and was not accepted. ⭐ **d2 AND d3 ARE COHERENT TOGETHER AND WERE PUT AS A POSSIBLE DEADLOCK, WHICH THEY ARE NOT.** The agent's slate said explicitly that *hold until green* combined with *do not re-run* is a deadlock, because `main` cannot go green without a src-touching merge and no src-touching merge can start while the hold stands. The operator took the re-run, which dissolves it: the hold discharges the moment the re-run reports green, and only then does `WBS-26.3` begin. REJECTED: start it now; hold and spend the session investigating `DEF-121` instead.

d4 - THE `WBS-26.2` VERDICT IS NOT TAKEN YET. The operator will read the generated slate (`tamheed-package/slice-review-slate.html`, `LL-011`) before ruling, rather than verdicting off the agent's summary. The row stays at `Review` and slice-scope `wbs-done` continues to name it, which is the rule working. ⚠ The agent offered `Implemented` as an option with its evidence attached and the operator did not take the shortcut - which is the `WBS-24.4` shape, where the per-item mechanism against a generated slate has already discriminated twice.
rationale:
WHY THE TWO OVERRIDES ARE RECORDED AS OVERRIDES RATHER THAN SMOOTHED INTO AGREEMENT, per the `DEC-071` d3 precedent. The agent recommended DO NOT RE-RUN and START `WBS-26.3`; the operator ruled RE-RUN and HOLD. A later session reading these clauses must not mistake either outcome for a consensus about the reasoning - the reasoning-against is preserved inside each clause for exactly that purpose, and it is the `DEC-067`/`DEC-094` shape a third time.

⚠⚠ THE PART THAT NEEDS WATCHING IS d2, AND IT IS NAMED HERE SO NOBODY HAS TO NOTICE IT LATER. `DEC-077` d3 has now been overridden TWICE IN TWO DAYS while remaining unconditional in its own text. The agent's third option - re-run AND amend d3 so the rule stops being unconditional-in-name-only - was offered precisely because accumulating overrides against a rule nobody follows is how a rule is repealed without anyone deciding to repeal it. That option was NOT taken, so d3 stands unconditional and this is the second override on its face. **A THIRD should reopen the question of whether the rule still says what the practice does.**

WHY THE ROW WAS FILED AS `DEF-121` RATHER THAN APPENDED TO `DEF-108`. `DEF-108` closed `Won't-fix` on 2026-08-30 (`DEC-097` d1) and its closing text instructs, in terms, that a further red from `SearchProvidersFtsTests` is a NEW finding to investigate on its own evidence: file a new defect, do not append to the closed row, and do not cite the closure as a precedent. That instruction was followed literally; `DEF-108` was not edited and a `relates_to` edge links the two rows.

HOW THE RED WAS FOUND, WHICH IS THE PROCESS HALF AND BELONGS IN THE RECORD. The merge of `#331` completed at 06:45:11Z; the following session prepared the resume and made three package commits without ever running `gh run list` against `main`. Measured: no progress-entry, defect, decision or deferred-work row in the package names run `33297623382`, while `PE-717` and `PE-718` record the build and the merge, and the kickoff prompt asserts `#331` merged *with ten checks green* - true of the PR run and false of the push run beside it. `DEC-077` d2 requires polling CI to completion after ANY push to `main`, and a squash-merge is such a push. **The rule failed on its first test after `DEF-108`'s hold was lifted, and the red sat unrecorded on `main` for a whole session.**

THE `LL-005` SWEEP RAN BEFORE THE INTERVIEW, NOT AFTER. Defects, deferred-work, decisions, ADRs, open-questions, risks, requirements, assumptions and lessons were PARSED AS JSON rather than regexed over JSONL - the FORTY-FIRST's cause - and the pass was calibrated, 114 rows matching a control term. It found `DEF-108`, `DW-084`, `DW-085` and `DEC-077`/`DEC-095`/`DEC-097` as the neighbours and nothing else in the package covering a SQL Server container that fails to start in CI. `RISK-019`, `DEF-021` and `DW-019` were checked and are unrelated. Both artifacts the operator read to decide were GENERATED and byte-verified against the canonical store (`LL-011`): `def-121-slate.html`, 9 blocks, verifier calibrated; `slice-review-slate.html` for `SL-035`.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-31 (TWELFTH ROUND, THE `DEF-122` REMEDY INTERVIEW): THE MECHANISM IS ISOLATED BEFORE ANY FIX IS WRITTEN, AND ONCE `main` IS GREEN THE SESSION CONTINUES STRAIGHT INTO `WBS-26.3`. THE FIRST RULING OVERRODE THE AGENT AGAIN, AND IT APPLIES `LL-029`'s STANDARD TO A DEFECT THE AGENT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN UP AS *CONSISTENT WITH* RATHER THAN *DIAGNOSED*.
decision:
d1 - `DEF-122` IS INVESTIGATED BEFORE IT IS FIXED. The window-rollover mechanism must be ISOLATED - an intervention that moves one variable and flips the outcome - not merely shown to be consistent with the evidence. Only then is a remedy chosen and written. OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, which was to warm the host outside the webhook partition and ship that to both rate-limit tests immediately, on the grounds that it is the smallest diff, keeps the integration property and adds no production surface. ⭐⭐ **THE RULING IS `LL-029` APPLIED TO THE AGENT'S OWN WRITE-UP.** `DEF-122`'s row says in terms that no variable was isolated and that the mechanism is a hypothesis; the agent then proposed a fix built on that hypothesis and offered isolation as the option NOT taken. **A remedy chosen from an unisolated cause is the THIRTY-FIFTH's shape** - there, a mechanism called *proven by reproduction* was confounded, the rival had been *measured and discarded* on a true number about a state that no longer held, and what finally caught it was the fix failing. ⚠ The agent's own recommendation carried an admitted residual - *it removes the DOMINANT cost, not every possible slow request* - which is a fix that cannot be falsified by the failure recurring, because a recurrence would be attributed to the residual rather than to the fix being wrong. REJECTED: warm the host outside the bucket; make the rate-limit window configurable; move the throttling assertion to a unit test over the limiter.

d2 - ONCE `DEF-122` IS FIXED AND `main` REPORTS GREEN, THE SESSION CONTINUES STRAIGHT INTO `WBS-26.3` WITHOUT A FURTHER ROUND TRIP. `DEC-100` d3's hold discharges the moment `main` is green and the next item is already fixed by `DEC-094` d5's order, so there is nothing left to decide at that boundary. MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION. ⚠ The pre-build sweep still runs first and still stops the build if it finds anything - it has changed the item before a line was written on BOTH `SL-035` items built so far, in a different direction each time (`WBS-26.1`'s found `FR-076` already specified SoD-4's COI half; `WBS-26.2`'s found its bound requirement covered neither signal AND that `DW-092`'s central data premise was false). REJECTED: report the green and wait; stop after the fix and start `WBS-26.3` in a fresh session.
rationale:
WHY d1 IS THE MORE CONSEQUENTIAL RULING, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THIS TEST. The cost of the rejected shortcut is not a wrong line of code - the warm-up fix would probably have worked. It is that **the register would have carried a fix whose stated basis was a hypothesis, on a row that says so in its own text**, and the next session reading `DEF-122` would find a remedy and a cause that were never connected by a measurement. This package has the instance already: `DEF-114`'s first diagnosis was confident, wrong, and had ALREADY discarded the true rival on a measurement taken against a state that no longer held. `LL-029` came out of that and is pinned: **a reproduction confirms; only an intervention that isolates one variable explains.**

WHAT ISOLATION MEANS HERE, RECORDED SO THE INVESTIGATION CAN BE JUDGED AGAINST IT RATHER THAN AGAINST ITS OWN CONCLUSION. The hypothesis is that the fixed window opens when the limiter's partition is first ACQUIRED - at the start of request 1, before the endpoint filter - so elapsed time INSIDE the window, not the test's total duration, is what decides the outcome. That predicts an asymmetry: **a delay longer than the window placed BETWEEN request 1 and request 2 flips the third response from 429 to 200, while a delay of the SAME LENGTH placed BEFORE request 1 changes nothing.** Both variants take the same wall-clock time, so *the test was slow* cannot explain a difference between them. ⚠ If both variants behave the same way, the hypothesis is wrong and the row must be rewritten rather than the fix adjusted.

⭐⭐ THE RE-RUN'S YIELD IS RECORDED AGAINST THE AGENT'S ARGUMENT, NOT AS A FOOTNOTE. `DEC-100` d2 was an override; the agent argued a re-run could produce no fact the register did not already hold, because a green on byte-identical code already existed on the PR head. **That argument was wrong, and it is what found `DEF-122`.** A re-run is not only a second sample of the question being asked; it is a fresh sample of every OTHER question the suite asks, and this one surfaced a latent defect in a test that had presumably passed hundreds of times. A later session must not read the preserved reasoning-against in `DEC-100` d2 as having been sound.

⚠ `DEF-121` IS UNAFFECTED BY ANY OF THIS AND DOES NOT MOVE. `SearchProvidersFtsTests` passed on the re-run (Integration 69 passed / 2 skipped / 71) and that discharges nothing: `DEC-100` d1 carried the row `Open`/high, and the rule inherited from `DEF-108` is that a backend integration failure is not called flaky on the strength of one more green. Package-scope readiness stays `ready:FALSE` on `DEF-121` throughout.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-31 (THIRTEENTH ROUND, THE `WBS-26.3` BUILD-SHAPE INTERVIEW): THE CHECK COVERS ALL THREE APPLICATION IMAGES, IT RUNS ON A REAL `docker compose build` IN `ci.yml`'s `compose` JOB, AND THE BASE ASSERTION IS A PROPERTY OF THE BUILT ARTIFACT RATHER THAN OF THE DOCKERFILE. ALL THREE RULINGS MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION - THE SECOND SUCH INTERVIEW IN THIS PROJECT, AND IT IS RECORDED BECAUSE THE OVERRIDE PATTERN IS OTHERWISE THE NORM.
decision:
d1 - THE CHECK COVERS ALL THREE APPLICATION IMAGES: `api`, `worker` AND `web`. `DW-090`'s sketch prescribed *"docker image inspect the api and worker images"* while `NFR-054`'s statement names *"ACMP's own application images - api, worker and web - shall not exceed 500 MB each"*, excluding only the database image from the size cap. **A check built to the row's words would have evidenced two-thirds of the requirement this item exists solely to make evidenceable**, producing a criterion that claims less than it appears to - the trap `DEC-092` already declined once when it refused to write an AC resting on a one-off local measurement. ⚠ `web` is also the image `ADR-0037` builds PER ENVIRONMENT, so it is the one most likely to drift unnoticed. ⚠⚠ **THIS IS AN AMENDMENT TO `DW-090`'s SKETCH AND NOT A SCOPE CHANGE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS DELIBERATE:** `WBS-26.3`'s own title is *the CI check that asserts image size AND base layer* and is unchanged, `NFR-054` already named three images before this interview, and `DW-090`'s two-image line sits under a heading reading *"what the check would be, since it is small"* - a sketch, not a specification. No `SC-` row is filed; `DW-090`'s text is corrected in place so the surviving copy is not the misleading one. REJECTED: two images as the row says, with `web` as a residual `DW-` row; three for size but two for base.

d2 - THE BUILD AND THE ASSERTIONS LIVE IN `ci.yml`'s `compose` JOB, ON A REAL `docker compose build api web worker`. **`DW-090` said *"after the compose build in CI"* and MEASURED, THERE IS NO COMPOSE BUILD IN CI** - the `compose` job runs `docker compose ... config -q` plus five node checks and builds nothing; it is a config validator whose name reads like a builder. `deploy/docker-compose.yml` already carries `build:` stanzas for `api`, `web`, `worker` and `sqlserver`, so one `docker compose build api web worker` yields exactly the three images `NFR-054` names and makes the row's own words true rather than aspirational. It sits beside the other deployment-artifact gates. ⚠ **THE COST IS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY:** that job runs **12 seconds** today and three image builds - `web`'s node/vite stage being the expensive one - will add minutes to EVERY PR, so `timeout-minutes: 10` must be raised in the same change. REJECTED: extending `security.yml`'s `trivy-image` job (cheapest, since it already builds `api`, but a compliance gate in the vulnerability workflow is a semantic mismatch and that job is deliberately `continue-on-error`, which a gate must never inherit); a new job on push-to-main only (**explicitly declined because a red would then arrive AFTER merge, which is exactly how `DEF-121` and `DEF-122` reached `main` in this very session**); a new dedicated job on every PR.

d3 - *"BASE IMAGE LAYER VERIFIED"* MEANS: `docker image inspect` the PULLED BASE image, take its `RootFS.Layers`, and assert they are a PREFIX of the BUILT image's `RootFS.Layers`. **This is a property of the ARTIFACT, not of the source that produced it.** It proves the image actually sits on that base and it is the only mechanical thing that would catch a digest bump silently dropping the `-extra` suffix. Costs one `docker pull` of each base. ⚠ **THE EXPECTED BASE IS PER-IMAGE, NOT ONE CONSTANT** - measured in `deploy/`: `api` and `worker` are both `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled-extra@sha256:f5b3b2e2...`, while `web` is `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31-alpine@sha256:334d9297...`. `DW-090`'s *"assert the base layer is the pinned chiseled-extra digest"* is true for two images and false for the third. REJECTED: asserting the Dockerfile's pinned `FROM` digest (**it verifies the SOURCE that built the image and not the image - circular, and it would pass even if the published artifact came from elsewhere; it must not be called *base image layer verified***); asserting on the image's config labels or history (cheaper, but history is not a guaranteed or stable surface across builders, so the check could go quietly vacuous after a buildx change - `DEF-078`'s blind-control shape).
rationale:
WHY THE SWEEP STOPPED THE BUILD, WHICH IS THE MECHANISM WORKING AND NOT A DELAY. `DEC-101` d2 authorised continuing straight into `WBS-26.3` without a further round trip, and said in the same clause that the pre-build sweep still runs first and still stops the build if it finds anything. **It found three things, and all three were invisible to every mechanical pass** - every identifier in `DW-090` resolves, every status is correct, `G-TRACE` is green. `LL-025`'s family: the row is a faithful description of a GAP and an unfaithful description of the REMEDY.

⭐⭐ **THE HABIT HAS NOW PAID ON ALL THREE `SL-035` ITEMS, IN A DIFFERENT DIRECTION EACH TIME.** `WBS-26.1`'s sweep found `FR-076` already specified SoD-4's COI half, so building it would have contradicted a requirement's own words. `WBS-26.2`'s found its bound requirement covered neither of its signals AND that `DW-092`'s central data premise was false - nothing recorded `Restricted`-topic reads at all. **This one finds the row's CENSUS exact and its PRESCRIPTION too small**, which is `WBS-24.4`'s shape. The census was re-verified rather than assumed: nothing in any workflow file or script asserts image size, and nothing asserts a base layer.

⚠⚠ THE FAILURE MODE d2 AVOIDS IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE AND IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY. Attaching an inspect step to the `compose` job as `DW-090`'s words literally suggest would have inspected images that job never built. On a warm runner `docker image inspect` can SUCCEED against a leftover image from an earlier run - so the gate would report compliance it never measured. **That is precisely the failure `DW-090` itself was filed about**: a size check alone passing on Debian at 326 MB while reporting compliance with a minimal-base clause from the base that clause excludes. A gate that inspects the wrong artifact is worse than no gate, because it is credited.

WHY THE BASE ASSERTION EARNS ITS COST, re-verified rather than remembered. `DEC-090`'s spike measured that plain chiseled and plain alpine ship no ICU, and that a .NET app on them starts, exits 0, and throws only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED - which this API never does. **A future digest bump that silently dropped `-extra` would render a Hijri date instead of a Gregorian one in Arabic, with no exception and no log line, and would pass every existing gate.** The base half is therefore the half that matters, and the size half alone is not the item. ⚠ `web`'s pinned digest is the subject of open Dependabot PR `#318`, which `DEC-083` d3 deliberately left alone, so the check's expected-base values must be maintainable rather than scattered.

⚠ NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS WRITTEN YET AND THAT IS DELIBERATE (trap 16c): a criterion written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently. `WBS-26.3`'s own row says to write it in the batch that produces the CI evidence, and `DEC-091` d1 records that this item's criterion-lessness up to now was deliberate rather than an omission. **This item is the route by which `NFR-054` becomes evidenceable for the first time.**

⚠ THE BUILD STILL WAITS ON `main` GOING GREEN. `DEC-100` d3's hold is discharged by a green `main`, not by this interview; `DEF-122`'s fix merged as `4529fd01` and its run was still in flight when these rulings were taken.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-31 (FOURTEENTH ROUND): `DEF-121` GETS `DEC-089`'s END-CONDITION STRUCTURE, THREE NEW LESSONS ARE CONFIRMED ONE BY ONE (TWO PINNED), `AC-088`..`AC-093` ARE INVESTIGATED BEFORE ANYTHING IS TOUCHED, AND THE SESSION BUILDS `WBS-26.3`. THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP PRODUCED THREE OF THE FOUR ITEMS AND TWO OF THEM WERE THE AGENT'S OWN GAPS.
decision:
d1 - `DEF-121` GETS A CHECKABLE END CONDITION, IN `DEC-089`'s CLAUSE STRUCTURE. Chased = (1) the cause is DIAGNOSED with evidence by an intervention that isolates a variable, or (2) an INSTRUMENTED RECURRENCE whose captured log names a cause, or (3) an explicit OPERATOR DISPOSITION. **Accumulated greens satisfy no clause, by design** - an end condition greens could satisfy would silently repeal the standing rule that a backend integration failure is not called flaky on the strength of one more green. MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION. ⚠⚠ **THE ITEM EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP MEASURED IT** (`LL-005`): probing `DEF-121` for *end condition*, *chased* and *clause (3)* returned ABSENT on all three while the same probes on `DEF-108` returned PRESENT, so the sole blocking failure in package-scope readiness had no stated way to end - **the exact failure `DEC-089` was written to prevent, reproduced one row later.** ⚠ The agent had offered an end condition at `DEC-100` and the operator chose carry-and-investigate over end-condition-FIRST; that ruling settled the disposition and left this half open rather than declining it. ⭐ **THE ROW ADDS A DISCRIMINATOR INSIDE CLAUSE (2) RATHER THAN A FOURTH CLAUSE:** a recurrence carrying THIS row's signature (`Reason 0x00000006`, errno 2 ENOENT, `AppLoader`-reported LOAD failure, no `lsasrv.dll`/`lsass.exe` frames) is a recurrence of THIS fault, while one carrying `DEF-108`'s occurrence-3/4 signature (`Reason 0x00000002`, errno 11 EAGAIN, `lsasrv.dll` + `lsass.exe` frames) is that closed row's family reappearing and is a separate finding - **record which, with the frames quoted, or the accumulation is uninterpretable.** REJECTED: a differently-shaped end condition; leaving it without one; converting or disposing of the row now instead.

d2 - THE THREE LESSONS ARE INTERVIEWED ONE BY ONE AND ALL THREE ARE APPROVED. **`LL-035` Approved + PINNED** - *a remedy that reduces a PROBABILITY cannot be falsified by the failure recurring; the recurrence gets attributed to the residual it openly admits.* **`LL-036` Approved + PINNED** - *a PR-head run and a merge-commit run are DIFFERENT runs over identical code, and `gh pr checks` only ever shows you the first; cite the run id, never a colour.* **`LL-037` Approved, NOT pinned** - *a re-run is not a second sample of the question you are asking, it is a fresh sample of every OTHER question the suite asks.* OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION ON THE SCHEDULING: the agent proposed leaving all three `Proposed` for a later ceremony on cost grounds, and the operator ran the interview now. The per-lesson verdicts then matched the agent's recommendations. ⚠⚠ **THE FILING ITSELF WAS A RECORDING-OBLIGATION MISS THE SWEEP CAUGHT:** measured before the interview, the register held **ZERO** `Proposed` lessons against 30 `Approved`, so `lessons-confirmed` was PASSING VACUOUSLY - a green control with no subject, `DEF-078`'s shape - while a session that had produced three durable findings had filed none of them. ✅ `handoff_emit` ran in the SAME batch as the approvals and the rebuilt note was verified to name all three, so `DEF-107`'s failure mode (a lesson approved, pinned and binding nothing for two days) did not recur. REJECTED: leaving them `Proposed` for a later ceremony; rejecting any of the three.

d3 - `AC-088`..`AC-093` ARE INVESTIGATED BEFORE ANYTHING IS TOUCHED. MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, and it is `DEC-101` d1's standard applied to the agent a second time: **the SHAPE of the anomaly is measured and its CAUSE is not.** Measured - six of 157 acceptance criteria sit at `Proposed` (135 are `Approved`, 16 `Superseded`), all six are contiguous, all six belong to `SL-028`, all six carry `Met` as their LATEST verdict, and `SL-028` itself is `Implemented`. `acs-met` passes because it reads verdicts and ignores `lifecycle_status`, so **nothing in the store has ever compared the two columns** - the unrelated-columns shape this package already records for `DW-` rows versus their `WBS-` items. ⚠ Checked against `LL-006`'s trap before being raised: `AC-089`, `AC-091` and `AC-093` are named by NO decision or ADR at all, so this is not `Proposed`-but-already-ruled (control: `DEF-121` returned three naming decisions in the same pass). ⛔ **PROMOTING IS ONE-WAY AND THAT IS WHY IT WAITS:** an `Approved` AC is immutable in this store and refuses edits including being marked superseded (`DEF-111`/`AC-147`), so a promotion made before the cause is known cannot be undone. Six contiguous rows from one slice is a PATTERN, not six oversights, and reading `SL-028`'s close and the `AV-124`..`AV-147` sequence is what distinguishes a repair from an erasure. REJECTED: promoting all six now; leaving them and recording the observation; leaving them and recording nothing.

d4 - THE SESSION BUILDS `WBS-26.3` NOW. `main` is GREEN at `4529fd01` (CI and Security both success), so `DEC-100` d3's hold is discharged, and `DEC-102` already settled the build's shape. OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION, which was to refresh the handoff and stop on the grounds that the session is long and expensive and that `WBS-26.3` would start clean in a fresh session with its shape already settled. ⚠ The agent's reasoning-against is preserved because the risk it named is real and now falls due: **`prm-next.md` currently records `#331` as merging *'with ten checks green'* and the memory index still says readiness is `FALSE` on `DEF-108`, both of which this session falsified** - and this project's own record is that writing the handoff LAST is what catches such drift. REJECTED: refresh the handoff and stop; build then refresh; apply `DEC-102` to `DW-090` and stop there.
rationale:
WHY THREE OF THE FOUR ITEMS CAME FROM THE SWEEP AND NOT FROM THE AGENDA, which is `LL-005` paying for the third recorded time. The session's own view of what was outstanding was `WBS-26.2`'s verdict and `WBS-26.3`'s build. The sweep - run BEFORE the interview, never after - produced `DEF-121`'s missing end condition, the vacuously-passing `lessons-confirmed` advisory, and the six `Proposed` criteria, **and two of those three were the agent's own gaps**: a lesson-filing obligation not discharged, and (found in the same pass, not put to the operator because it is unambiguously drift rather than a decision) `DEC-102` d1's in-place correction to `DW-090` never applied - an approved decision whose delta was never merged, which no advisory catches because `scope-changes-merged` watches `SC-` rows and not `DEC-` rows.

⭐⭐ THE PATTERN ACROSS d1 AND d3 IS ONE RULE APPLIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. d1 exists because a HOLD without a checkable end cannot end; d3 exists because an IRREVERSIBLE promotion without a known cause cannot be undone. Both are refusals to act on a measured shape whose mechanism is unmeasured, and d3 is the operator applying to the agent's proposal exactly the standard `DEC-101` d1 applied to the agent's `DEF-122` fix a few hours earlier. **The agent recommended investigation in d3 having been taught it in `DEC-101`** - which is the intended effect of a ruling and is recorded so it reads as transfer rather than coincidence.

⚠ WHAT d4 ACCEPTS KNOWINGLY. Building `WBS-26.3` before refreshing `prm-next.md` means the kickoff prompt carries claims this session falsified for the duration of the build, and if the session ends inside the build they persist. The operator ruled to build; the obligation to refresh the prompt and the memory index survives the ruling and is the session's closing act, not an optional one.

title: OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-31 (FIFTEENTH ROUND): `DEF-123`'s BLANKET TEST EDGES ARE INVESTIGATED FOR SEMANTICS AND NOT ONLY FOR PROVENANCE, `TEST-054` IS PROMOTED AND ITS FALSE TEXT CORRECTED, BOTH OWED VERDICTS GO TO A REGENERATED SLATE, AND THE SESSION APPROVES `LL-038`/`LL-039` THEN BUILDS `WBS-26.4`. THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP PRODUCED BOTH REGISTER FINDINGS; NEITHER WAS ON THE AGENDA.
decision:
d1 - `DEF-123` IS INVESTIGATED FOR **SEMANTICS**, NOT ONLY FOR PROVENANCE. **OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION**, which was to sweep progress entries for `TEST-041`/`TEST-045` and stop there. The operator required the stronger pass: sweep the provenance AND then **sample the blanket edges and judge which are defensible against which are not** - a core-loop E2E can plausibly bear on latency, availability and usability clauses; it cannot bear on `NFR-054` (images built from a minimal base, ≤ 500 MB), `NFR-052` (single-command `docker compose up`) or `NFR-018` (an external assessor's ASVS report). **The deliverable is a real count of false claims rather than a shape.** ⚠ The agent's reasoning-against is preserved: the provenance sweep is cheap and could have shown the whole block was a considered position, making the semantic pass unnecessary. The operator's reading is that a count is what a disposition needs either way. ⛔ **NO EDGE IS TOUCHED BY THIS RULING** - deleting the blanket edges would turn `G-TRACE` red for 63 requirements at once, and `DEF-123`'s own text argues against choosing a remedy before the count exists. REJECTED: sweep progress entries first then decide; carry it Open at medium with no investigation; scope the re-wiring as a `DW-` row now.

d2 - `TEST-054` IS PROMOTED TO `Implemented` (verdict `Pass`) AND ITS TEXT IS CORRECTED. MATCHED THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION. Its title asserted *"PLANNED, NOT YET WRITTEN"* while `tests/Acmp.Api.Tests/AnomalySignalAuditTests.cs` exists with four facts, is cited by `AC-157`/`AV-235` by filename, and has passed CI three times (runs `33297623382`, `33391609531`, `33392572509`). ⭐ **TRAP 16f'S WARNING RAN IN REVERSE.** It says a `Proposed` test row *"must never read as evidence that a test exists"*; the fault that actually occurred is the inverse - once the test was written the row read as evidence that it did **not**. **Nothing compares a test row's `lifecycle_status` to the existence of the file it names**, which is the same unrelated-columns shape this package already records for `DW-` rows versus their `WBS-` items and for an AC's `lifecycle_status` versus its verdicts. REJECTED: correct the text but leave it `Proposed`; leave it entirely.

d3 - BOTH OWED VERDICTS GO TO A REGENERATED SLATE AND ARE NOT TAKEN IN THIS ROUND. `node scripts/gen-slice-review-slate.mjs SL-035` now renders `WBS-26.2` and `WBS-26.3` with `AC-157`/`AV-236` and `AC-158`/`AV-237` quoted byte-identically. The operator declined the offered shortcut of promoting both on the agent's summary - `LL-011`, and the per-item mechanism has discriminated twice before on `WBS-24.4`. Both rows stay at `Review`; slice-scope `wbs-done` keeps naming them, which is the rule working. REJECTED: implement both now; implement one and withhold the other; defer to a dedicated review session.

d4 - `LL-038` AND `LL-039` ARE APPROVED, AND THE SESSION THEN BUILDS `WBS-26.4`. **OVERRODE THE AGENT'S RECOMMENDATION TO STOP AFTER THE APPROVALS**, which rested on session length and cost. `LL-038` (a lifecycle status can be load-bearing rather than lagging) is **PINNED** - it stopped an irreversible promotion of six acceptance criteria hours after being learned, and it applies to any register work. `LL-039` (`skipped` conflates *the `if:` was false* with *a needed job did not succeed*) is approved **UNPINNED** - it is sharp but narrow, following `LL-037`'s precedent from `DEC-103` d2; the operator ruled the approvals and the pin split follows the pattern they set there, and is stated here so it can be corrected rather than inferred. `handoff_emit` runs in the SAME batch (`DEF-107`). ⚠ **`WBS-26.4` IS THE RISKY ONE AND ITS OWN ROW SAYS SO:** `/readyz` reaches SQL Server, Hangfire and object storage, so switching the api dependents to `service_healthy` can turn a slow cold boot into a failed stack. **Prove the failure mode BOTH ways; a green run proves nothing about that control.** REJECTED: approve and stop; leave the lessons `Proposed` and stop; stop recording nothing further.
rationale:
BOTH REGISTER FINDINGS CAME FROM THE PRE-INTERVIEW SWEEP AND NEITHER WAS ON THE AGENDA - `LL-005` paying for the fourth recorded time, and the third time it caught something the agent had not thought to look for. The session's own view of what was outstanding was two verdicts and two lessons.

⭐⭐ THE SWEEP THAT FOUND `DEF-123` WAS BUILT IN RESPONSE TO THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S MISS, AND IT FOUND A DIFFERENT THING THAN IT WAS BUILT FOR. `DEC-103` recorded that `DEC-102` d1's promised in-place correction to `DW-090` had never been applied - **an approved decision whose delta was never merged, which no advisory catches because `scope-changes-merged` watches `SC-` rows and not `DEC-` rows.** So this round swept approved decisions for language promising a row edit. It found `DEC-095` making exactly such a promise, and **that one HAD been honoured** (`DW-093` carries `SC-039` and the correction). **The check came back clean on its own subject and the run that produced it surfaced the test-edge blanket instead** - which is `LL-013`'s point inverted: a scanner proven to have a subject is worth running even when its answer is negative, because looking is what finds the adjacent thing.

⚠ WHY d1 MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS. `DEF-123`'s concrete instance is from this session: `DW-090` and `DEC-092` both recorded that `NFR-054` **could not be evidenced** because no CI check existed - measured twice and true - while the trace register simultaneously asserted `NFR-054` **was tested**, by two edges, one of them from a suite that has not been written. **The package held both claims at once and nothing compared them.** `G-TRACE` and `G-REL` pass and are correct to: the edges exist and their relation types are legal. **`G-REL` validates an edge's shape; no rule validates its claim.**

⚠ WHAT d1 DOES NOT AUTHORISE. It is an investigation, not a repair. No edge is deleted, re-pointed or added under this ruling, and `TEST-045` is not written. `DEF-123`'s text records why picking a remedy now would be wrong - deleting the blanket turns `G-TRACE` red for 63 requirements at once, re-wiring individually is unscoped, and writing one suite fixes one edge of 129 - and `LL-035` is explicit that a remedy which reduces a problem without removing its condition cannot be falsified by the condition persisting.
